Fact.Name: Return files Form 4797
Fact.Description: True when at least one of the Part I section 1231, Part II ordinary-disposition, or Part III section 1245 disposition collections contains an entry. Each collection is checked only after its own completeness guard; seeded empty collections contribute false, while an unanswered collection remains incomplete unless another collection already proves that Form 4797 is filed.

Fact.Name: Has a section 1245 depreciation-recapture disposition to report on Form 4797 Part III
Fact.Description: Whether the return reports one or more dispositions of section 1245 property (depreciable personalty) that trigger depreciation recapture on Form 4797 Part III. Gate for the intake; when true the /section1245Dispositions collection carries one item per disposition. When absent or false the whole module resolves Complete-0 (additive).

Fact.Name: Claims a section 1245 depreciation-recapture disposition
Fact.Description: Complete-safe gate: true only when /hasSection1245Disposition is answered and true (the IsComplete pattern, as /claimsCasualtyLoss). Unanswered resolves Complete-false so every return without a section 1245 disposition still resolves and keeps every aggregate Complete-0 (every existing scenario that never populates /section1245Dispositions stays byte-identical).

Fact.Name: Section 1245 property dispositions
Fact.Description: The collection of section 1245 property dispositions reported on Form 4797 Part III (one item per property disposed, Form 4797 lines 19 to 25b). Each item holds the per-property inputs (gross sales price, cost or other basis, depreciation allowed, the section 1245 personalty attestation, and the holding-period attestation) and the per-property recapture + section 1231 split. SIMPLIFICATION: one property per item; the form's four property columns (A to D) are entered as separate items.

Fact.Name: Section 1245 disposition description (stable identity)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 19 column (a), the description of the property. Plays no part in any computation. SCREEN SPEC - this is the screen that decides which table a disposition belongs in. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Describe the property." HELP TEXT: "Use this table ONLY for section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 property - for example depreciable equipment, vehicles and buildings, farm land on which soil or water expenses were deducted, oil, gas or other mineral property, and section 126 cost-sharing property. Bare land is none of these: report it in the Part I line 2 table if you held it more than 1 year, or in the Part II line 10 table if you held it 1 year or less. If you sold a building together with its land, split the sale - the building here, the land in the Part I line 2 table." The split rule is the instructions' own ("report the sale of a building in Part III and the land in Part I", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 2, right column) and the chart routes other farmland to Part I or Part II, never to Part III (row 5, line 43). ASKED WHEN: once per Part III disposition. UNANSWERED: OPTIONAL (three-state); the item is unlabeled and no number changes. VALIDATION: text, at most 100 characters. WHAT IT FEEDS: the printed line 19(a) cell only.

Fact.Name: Property is section 1245 personalty (scope attestation)
Fact.Description: Whether the disposed property is SECTION 1245 property (depreciable or amortizable PERSONALTY, e.g. machinery, equipment, vehicles, furniture) as opposed to SECTION 1250 real property (buildings and their structural components). Section 1245 recapture is the smaller of the depreciation allowed and the gain realized (Form 4797 line 25b). Section 1250 real property uses a different recapture block (lines 26a to 26g plus the unrecaptured-section- 1250-gain / 28% worksheets). The taxpayer attests the section 1245 character; the engine gates on the attestation. THIS FACT ANSWERED FALSE STOPPED BEING THE REFUSAL TRIGGER ON 2026-08-04, and the sentence that said otherwise is corrected here rather than left to contradict the gate. It read "because the knockout fires on the whole NON-attested complement, every non-section-1245 class that is entered (land, section 1252 farmland, section 1254 mineral interests, section 1255 cost-sharing property) is refused, not just section 1250 buildings". The complement is now narrower by EXACTLY ONE class and no more: ../isSection1250Property is the second arm of the same printed column (Form 4797 line 19(a) is "Description of section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254, or 1255 property"), an item is admitted when it attests EITHER class, and everything else - LAND, and an item that attests none of the five class questions - is refused (section 1254, section 1252 and section 1255 property are admitted by their own class attestations). A FALSE answer here is now a legitimate state that ../isSection1250Property is expected to complete, not a refusal on its own. WHICH ARM WINS IF BOTH ARE ANSWERED TRUE: this one. A property cannot be both classes, and ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution's Switch tests the section 1245 arm FIRST, so a contradictory item recaptures ALL depreciation (line 25b) rather than only the excess (line 26g) and contributes nothing to the 25% rate group. For a TRUTHFULLY ENTERED pair line 25b is never smaller than line 26g for the same property, because the excess of actual over straight-line depreciation cannot exceed the total depreciation - so the precedence is the conservative one. THE TREE DOES NOT ENFORCE THAT INEQUALITY and this sentence does not claim it does: ../writableAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975 carries a Min 0 and no cap at ../depreciationAllowed, deliberately (line 26a is not capped on the printed form; line 26b applies the only cap the form draws, against line 24). A filer who enters an impossible line 26a above their own line 22 makes line 26g the larger figure and inverts the ordering - and every consequence of that stays taxpayer-adverse or neutral: MORE ordinary income under the section 1250 arm, and ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent floored at zero rather than negative. LIVESTOCK is the one truthfully-attestable section 1245 personalty class this question cannot police (24-/12-month section 1231 thresholds) - it is carved out by the separate ../isLivestock attestation.

Fact.Name: Property is section 1250 depreciable real property (scope attestation, the second arm of the Part III class column)
Fact.Description: Whether the disposed property is SECTION 1250 property - "depreciable real property (other than section 1245 property)" (2025 Instructions for Form 4797, Line 26), i.e. buildings and their structural components. THE SECOND ARM OF ONE PRINTED COLUMN, not a second table: Form 4797 line 19(a) is "Description of section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254, or 1255 property", lines 20 through 24 are the same six columns for all five classes, and only the recapture block below them differs by class (line 25 for section 1245, line 26 for section 1250, lines 27, 28 and 29 for the rest). The shipping collection modeled that column with ../isSection1245Property alone, whose FALSE branch was refused rather than classed; this fact classes one more of it. SECTION 1250 RECAPTURE IS NOT SECTION 1245 RECAPTURE, which is the whole reason the class needs its own arm rather than a wider gate. Section 1245 recaptures ALL the depreciation allowed or allowable (line 25b = the smaller of line 24 and line 25a); section 1250 recaptures only the EXCESS of actual depreciation over straight line (../writableAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975, line 26a), and the rest of the depreciation becomes UNRECAPTURED SECTION 1250 GAIN taxed in the 25% rate group (../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent). Admitting a section 1250 item into the section 1245 arm would over-recapture; refusing it computes nothing at all. Both were wrong, and this is the fork that makes neither necessary. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered is read as FALSE through ../isSection1250PropertyComplete, which leaves the item exactly where it stood before this fact existed - an item attesting NEITHER class still fails ../isInScope and still refuses, as land, section 1252 farmland, section 1254 mineral interests and section 1255 cost-sharing property do. ANSWERING TRUE COSTS ONE MORE ANSWER: an attested section 1250 item whose line 24 is a GAIN must also answer line 26a, or ../hasUnansweredAdditionalDepreciationGain refuses it. See that fact for why zero is not a default the graph may take on the filer's behalf. THE THREE REMAINING PRINTED CLASSES ARE NOT ADMITTED. Line 27 (section 1252 farmland), line 28 (section 1254 oil, gas, geothermal and mineral) and line 29 (section 1255 section 126 cost-sharing) keep failing the gate through the non-attestation complement. This fact admits ONE new class; it does not silently widen to five. THAT PARAGRAPH IS ONE CLASS OUT OF DATE AS OF 2026-08-17 and is corrected here rather than left for a reader to find: ../isSection1254Property now admits LINE 28 on the same shape, so the classes still failing the gate are line 27 (section 1252 farmland), line 29 (section 1255 section 126 cost-sharing) and land. TWO remain, not three.

Fact.Name: Property is section 1254 oil, gas, geothermal or other mineral property (scope attestation, the third arm of the Part III class column)
Fact.Description:
Whether the disposed property is SECTION 1254 property - an interest in oil, gas, geothermal or other mineral property whose intangible drilling and development costs, mine exploration and development costs, or depletion were deducted rather than capitalized. THE THIRD ARM OF ONE PRINTED COLUMN, on the shape ../isSection1250Property established. Form 4797 line 19(a) is "Description of section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254, or 1255 property", lines 20 through 24 are the same six columns for all five classes, and only the recapture block below them differs by class - line 25 for section 1245, line 26 for section 1250, line 28 for this one. This fact classes one more of the complement that used to refuse. SECTION 1254 RECAPTURE IS ITS OWN RULE AND IS NOT EITHER SIBLING'S. Section 1245 recaptures the DEPRECIATION allowed or allowable; section 1250 recaptures only the EXCESS of actual depreciation over straight line and sends the rest to the 25% rate group; section 1254 recaptures the EXPENDITURES the taxpayer chose to deduct instead of capitalize - IRC 1254(a)(1)(A), "expenditures which have been deducted by the taxpayer or any person under section 263, 616, or 617 with respect to such property and which, but for such deduction, would have been included in the adjusted basis of such property" plus "the deductions for depletion under section 611 which reduced the adjusted basis of such property" - capped by (a)(1)(B) at the gain. None of the three is a widening of another, which is why the class needs its own arm rather than a looser gate on an existing one. THERE IS NO UNRECAPTURED-GAIN TAIL HERE, which is the structural difference from the section 1250 arm worth stating on the fact rather than leaving to arithmetic. The Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 1 says "a section 1250 property"; a section 1254 item is not one, so ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent is $0 for it and the whole non-recapture remainder is a section 1231 amount. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered is read as FALSE through ../isSection1254PropertyComplete, so an item that answered only the section 1245 or section 1250 question before this fact existed reads false here and is untouched. An item attesting NO class still fails ../isInScope and still refuses, as bare land does.
ANSWERING TRUE COSTS ONE MORE ANSWER: an attested section 1254 item whose line 24 is a GAIN must also answer line 28a, or ../hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain refuses it. See that fact for why zero is not a default the graph may take on the filer's behalf. A MULTI-CLASS ITEM REFUSES, and it refuses on BOTH pairs - section 1254 with section 1250, and section 1254 with section 1245. The first cut of this change instead let the Switch position decide and disclosed that as an accepted limit; adversarial review the same day showed the limit was not direction-safe, and the disposition is now ../hasContradictorySection1254ClassAttestation, which carries the full argument. In one line: no printed inequality orders line 28b against either line 26g (structurally $0 for post-1986 MACRS and straight-line realty, so the old precedence could report $0 where line 28b was the entire gain) or line 25b (line 22 carries the section 611 depletion but not the section 263(c)/616/617 costs, which never entered basis, so 25b can be far smaller than 28b) - and the printed line 31 would ADD the blocks rather than choose between them. THE SECTION 1245 / SECTION 1250 PAIR IS UNAFFECTED and keeps its precedence, because that one IS provable: line 25b is never smaller than line 26g for the same property.

Fact.Name: Property is section 1252 farm land (scope attestation, the fourth arm of the Part III class column)
Fact.Description: Whether the disposed property is SECTION 1252 property - farm land for which deductions were allowed under section 175 (soil and water conservation expenditures) and which the taxpayer has held for LESS THAN 10 YEARS. THE FOURTH ARM OF ONE PRINTED COLUMN, on the shape ../isSection1250Property established and ../isSection1254Property repeated. Form 4797 line 19(a) is "Description of section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254, or 1255 property", lines 20 through 24 are the same six columns for all five classes, and only the recapture block below them differs by class - line 25 for section 1245, line 26 for section 1250, line 27 for this one, line 28 for section 1254, line 29 for section 1255. SECTION 1252 RECAPTURE IS ITS OWN RULE. Section 1245 recaptures the DEPRECIATION allowed or allowable; section 1250 recaptures only the EXCESS over straight line; section 1254 recaptures the deducted EXPENDITURES in full; section 1252 recaptures an AGE-DISCOUNTED share of the section 175 deductions - IRC 1252(a)(1)(A), "the applicable percentage of the aggregate of the deductions allowed under section 175 ... for expenditures made by the taxpayer with respect to the farm land" - capped by (a)(1)(B) at the gain. The applicable percentage is what makes this class different from all three of its siblings, and it lives on ../section1252Line27b. THE 10-YEAR CEILING IS NOT A SEPARATE GATE HERE. The statute applies only to farm land "held for less than 10 years" and the table gives 0 percent from the tenth year onward, so a longer-held farm land item attesting this class computes a line 27c of zero and its whole gain stays a section 1231 amount - which is exactly where the chart's row 5 ("All other farmland used in a trade or business") sends it. Admitting it is therefore not a widening of the modeled population in any direction that moves a number. THE PRINTED PARTNERSHIP EXCLUSION IS THE FILER'S. Line 27's own caption says to skip the section "if this form is being completed for a partnership"; this dictionary files individual returns only, so the exclusion is satisfied by the form the graph is filling. NO UNRECAPTURED-GAIN TAIL. The Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 1 says "a section 1250 property"; farm land is not one, so ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent is $0 for this item and the whole non-recapture remainder is a section 1231 amount. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered is read as FALSE through ../isSection1252PropertyComplete, so every item committed before this fact existed is untouched. An item attesting NO class still fails ../isInScope and still refuses, as bare land does. ANSWERING TRUE COSTS ONE MORE ANSWER inside the percentage bands: an attested section 1252 item whose line 24 is a GAIN must also answer line 27a, or ../hasUnansweredSection1252ExpensesGain refuses it - unless ../farmlandFullYearsHeld is 9 or more, where the instructions themselves say to skip line 27 and the unanswered figure cannot change a number. A MULTI-CLASS ITEM REFUSES through ../hasContradictoryFarmlandOrCostSharingClassAttestation, which carries the argument. WITH ONE EXCEPTION. The section 1252 + section 1255 farm land - the one pair the printed instructions DO order - is now COMPUTED in that order, line 27c then line 29b on the gain remaining after it, and both blocks reach the printed line 31. The sentence above stood until that date and is otherwise unchanged: section 1252 attested alongside section 1245, section 1250 or section 1254 still refuses.

Fact.Name: Property is section 1255 section 126 cost-sharing property (scope attestation, the fifth arm of the Part III class column)
Fact.Description: Whether the disposed property is SECTION 1255 property - property "acquired, improved, or otherwise modified by the application of payments excluded from gross income under section 126" (IRC 1255(a)(2)). THE FIFTH AND LAST ARM of the printed line 19(a) class column, which closes the enumeration the module has been filling one class at a time since 2026-08-04. SECTION 1255 RECAPTURE IS ITS OWN RULE and it is the only one of the five whose PRINTED LINE ASKS FOR THE PRODUCT RATHER THAN THE FACTORS. Line 29a is "Applicable percentage of payments excluded from income under section 126", not the payments themselves; line 29b is the smaller of line 24 or 29a. There is no line 29c. So the graph takes ONE dollar carry-in and performs ONE minimum - the ../isSection1254Property block's shape exactly - while the section 1252 block above takes TWO inputs and performs the multiplication itself, because line 27 prints 27a, 27b and 27c as three separate lines. The difference between the two new blocks is the form's, not this module's. WHERE THE PERCENTAGE WENT, since it is a real rule and this fact does not compute it: IRC 1255(a)(3) is 100 percent for a disposition less than 10 years after the section 126 payments were received, then "100 percent reduced (but not below zero) by 10 percent for each year or part thereof in excess of 10 years", reaching zero in the twentieth year. The instructions print the same rule. It is the FILER'S to apply, disclosed here rather than hidden in a default, for the reason the printed line gives: the form asks for one number and this graph holds no receipt date to count from. See ../writableSection1255ApplicablePercentageOfPayments. NO UNRECAPTURED-GAIN TAIL and no depreciation tie: section 126 property is not section 1250 property, so ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent is $0 for this item. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered is read as FALSE through ../isSection1255PropertyComplete, so every item committed before this fact existed is untouched. ANSWERING TRUE COSTS ONE MORE ANSWER: an attested section 1255 item whose line 24 is a GAIN must also answer line 29a, or ../hasUnansweredSection1255PaymentsGain refuses it. Unlike the section 1252 twin there is no printed band in which the answer stops mattering, so the guard carries no exception. A MULTI-CLASS ITEM REFUSES through ../hasContradictoryFarmlandOrCostSharingClassAttestation. For this class the refusal was the one that cost something real: the Line 29b instruction prints an ORDERING for exactly this case, and the section 1252 + section 1255 farm land is a population the IRS expects. That refusal, and what a successor owed it, are stated on the guard. THAT SUCCESSOR IS BUILT and the section 1252 + section 1255 pair is no longer refused. ../section1255OrdinaryRecaptureContribution performs the printed Line 29b reduction - line 24 less line 27c, then the minimum against line 29a - and ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution adds the two blocks in a case of its own. Section 1255 attested alongside section 1245, section 1250 or section 1254 still refuses.

Fact.Name: Property held more than one year (holding-period attestation)
Fact.Description: Whether the property was held more than one year (Form 4797 Part III line 19 date columns). Section 1245 ORDINARY recapture (line 25b) is INDEPENDENT of the holding period, so this does NOT change the recapture amount. It DOES drive the routing of the non-recapture REMAINDER (the section 1231 excess or loss): held more than one year -> Form 4797 Part I section 1231 (netted, then split ordinary/long-term capital gain); held one year or less -> Form 4797 Part II ORDINARY gain/(loss). ASKED WHEN the two Part III line 19 date columns (../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired, ../writableLineNineteenDateSold) are not both entered; with both dates entered the holding period is derived from them (../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates) and an answer here, if given, still governs. UNANSWERED with the dates not both entered: a GAIN takes no default - its routing and every total it feeds stay Incomplete and the return does not complete until the question is answered (../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete); a LOSS REFUSES the item (../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss knocks it out of ../isInScope), because routing it to Part II would bypass the section 1231 netting against answered long-term gains and suppress the section 1231(c) lookback entry. The form has no "unknown" branch: the instructions prescribe how to COUNT the period, so the datum is always knowable by the taxpayer.

Fact.Name: Property is livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy, or sporting purposes (carve-out attestation)
Fact.Description: Whether the disposed property is LIVESTOCK (cattle, horses, or other livestock, but not poultry) used in a trade or business and held for draft, breeding, dairy, or sporting purposes. Such livestock IS depreciable section 1245 personalty, but its section 1231 holding threshold is 24 MONTHS (cattle and horses) or 12 MONTHS (other livestock), not the "more than 1 year" test this module applies uniformly - the routing chart sends cattle/horses held less than 24 months to Part II (ordinary) where the uniform test would split recapture-then-section-1231 (taxpayer-favorable LTCG on a 13-to-23-month gain). SINCE 2026-07-31 those thresholds ARE modeled rather than refused wholesale: TRUE routes the item onto ../writableIsCattleOrHorses and ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths, and an item that meets its own threshold (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet) is IN scope and computes. SINCE 2026-08-03 an item that does NOT meet its threshold is in scope too, routed to Part II as ordinary income exactly as chart rows 7a/7b and 8a/8b print (../livestockPartIIOrdinaryRouting). The only livestock item that still REFUSES is a SUB-THRESHOLD LOSS whose month count or class question is unanswered (../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss), because routing such a loss to Part II would bypass the section 1231 netting on the strength of an input nobody stated. OPTIONAL (three-state). ASKED WHEN: every section 1245 disposition sold at a GAIN whose holding period could fall in the window where the livestock test and the general test disagree (from the 12-month anniversary up to the 24-month anniversary) - that is, unless both line 19 dates are entered and show under 12 months or 24 months or more. UNANSWERED there: NO default - the item's routing and every total it feeds stay Incomplete until the question is answered (../isLivestockComplete). UNANSWERED elsewhere reads as not livestock, because the answer cannot change a number: a non-section 1245 class, property IRC 1231(b)(1) excludes or de minimis property (Part II whatever the holding period), a date-bounded holding period outside the window, or a LOSS (which keeps the not-livestock reading, the section 1231 netting it then stays in being the adverse direction for a loss). This is a property-class question, so the dates cannot answer it; they can only show that it does not matter. RAISED VERSUS PURCHASED IS NOT MODELLED, AND DELIBERATELY SO. Chart rows 7c and 8c route "Raised cattle and horses sold at a gain" and "Raised livestock sold at a gain" to Part I even past the threshold, where rows 7a and 8a route the purchased animal to Part III (1245). The contract this change filled proposed either adding a raised-versus-purchased attestation or refusing raised livestock explicitly; on re-examination NEITHER is needed, because the two rows already agree numerically under this module's own arithmetic. A raised animal was never capitalized, so it carries no ../depreciationAllowed - and Part III line 25b is the smaller of the gain and the depreciation, which is 0 when the depreciation is 0, leaving the WHOLE gain as ../nonRecaptureRemainder and routing it to Part I exactly as row 7c prescribes. The distinction is presentational (which line of the form the figure is entered on), not computational, and it is SELF-CORRECTING rather than assumed: recapture can only fire where there is depreciation to recapture, and an animal carrying depreciation is not a row-7c animal. A raised-versus-purchased writable would therefore add an intake that changes no number, and refusing raised livestock would need that same writable in order to refuse returns the arithmetic already handles correctly.

Fact.Name: Livestock is cattle or horses (the 24-month section 1231 threshold, not the 12-month one)
Fact.Description: WHICH of the two livestock section 1231 holding thresholds this animal is measured against. IRC section 1231(b)(3) splits livestock in two: (A) CATTLE AND HORSES, regardless of age, held for draft, breeding, dairy, or sporting purposes and held "for 24 months or more from the date of acquisition"; (B) OTHER LIVESTOCK, regardless of age, on the same purpose test but held "for 12 months or more". The 2025 Instructions for Form 4797 routing chart carries the same split as its rows 7 ("Cattle and horses ... Held less than 24 months" vs "Held 24 months or more") and 8 ("Livestock other than cattle and horses ... Held less than 12 months" vs "Held 12 months or more"). Poultry is neither - section 1231(b)(3)'s closing sentence excludes it, as does ../isLivestock's own definition. ONLY MEANINGFUL on an item whose ../isLivestock is answered TRUE; on any other disposition nothing reads the threshold this selects. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered is read as CATTLE OR HORSES, i.e. the LONGER 24-month threshold - see ../appliesCattleOrHorseThreshold for the direction rationale.

Fact.Name: Months the livestock was held (section 1231(b)(3) counts MONTHS, not years)
Fact.Description: How many whole MONTHS the taxpayer held this animal, counted from the date of acquisition, for the section 1231(b)(3) livestock test. A SECOND holding-period intake beside ../heldMoreThanOneYear, not a replacement for it, because the two ask different questions and neither answers the other: section 1231(b)(3) measures livestock in months ("24 months or more", "12 months or more") while ../heldMoreThanOneYear is the general more-than-one-year test, and a Boolean at one year cannot express either livestock threshold. The gap is not academic in EITHER direction - a 13-to-23-month animal answers TRUE to "held more than 1 year" and yet fails the 24-month cattle test, and an animal held exactly 12 months PASSES section 1231(b)(3)(B) while answering FALSE to "more than 1 year" (a holding period is more than one year only from the day after the one-year anniversary). ../heldMoreThanOneYear therefore keeps its own meaning and its own consumers unchanged; on a livestock item the section 1231 routing reads this count instead (../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod). ONLY MEANINGFUL on an item whose ../isLivestock is answered TRUE. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered with both Part III line 19 dates entered, the section 1231(b)(3) test is taken from the dates (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet: ../heldTwentyFourMonthsOrMoreByDates or ../heldTwelveMonthsOrMoreByDates, the anniversary qualifying); unanswered with the dates not both entered, a GAIN takes no default - its routing stays Incomplete until answered - and a LOSS is refused (../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss). NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit).

Fact.Name: Gross sales price (Form 4797 Part III line 20)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 20: the gross sales price (amount realized) on this disposition of section 1245 property.

Fact.Name: Cost or other basis plus expense of sale (Form 4797 Part III line 21)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 21: the cost or other basis of the property plus the expense of sale (before subtracting depreciation). Line 23 adjusted basis = line 21 minus line 22.

Fact.Name: Depreciation allowed or allowable (Form 4797 Part III lines 22 and 25a)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 22 (also line 25a): the depreciation (or depletion) allowed or allowable on this property since acquisition, including any section 179 expense and MACRS deductions. This is both the reduction to adjusted basis (line 23) and the ceiling on the ordinary recapture (line 25b = smaller of line 24 or line 25a).

Fact.Name: Depreciation allowed or allowable, nonnegative (Form 4797 Part III lines 22 and 25a)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 22 (also line 25a) is an allowed-or-allowable depreciation or depletion total. The printed figure cannot be negative: an aggregate of depreciation or depletion allowed is a nonnegative amount, and the writable's Min-0 declaration is not enforced when a dependent fact resolves it. This complete-safe alias therefore floors ../depreciationAllowed at $0 before the amount reduces adjusted basis, enters line 22/25a, or caps ordinary recapture. It is the same entered figure when the answer is valid and changes only an impossible negative answer.

Fact.Name: Additional depreciation after 1975 (Form 4797 Part III line 26a, carry-IN)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 26a, "Additional depreciation after 1975", which the instructions define as "the excess of actual depreciation (including any special depreciation allowance, or commercial revitalization deduction) over depreciation figured using the straight line method" for the period after 1975. ONLY MEANINGFUL on an item whose ../isSection1250Property is answered TRUE; nothing reads it on any other disposition. A CARRY-IN ATTESTATION, NOT A COMPUTATION, and the reason is structural rather than stylistic: the excess needs a per-year depreciation history and a straight-line recomputation of the same property over the same recovery period, and this graph holds neither. ../depreciationAllowed is the TOTAL allowed-or-allowable figure (line 22, also line 25a); line 26a needs it SPLIT, which no shipping fact can do. Same posture as /writableNonrecapturedSection1231Loss and /writableSection1231GainFromInstallmentSales. NOT CAPPED HERE. Line 26b applies its own minimum against line 24, so line 26a itself is free to exceed the gain; the cap that matters is on the recapture, not on the input. OPTIONAL (three-state), and the unanswered direction is NOT a silent zero. On an item whose line 24 is a GAIN, unanswered REFUSES through ../hasUnansweredAdditionalDepreciationGain; on a loss or a zero-gain item it reads as $0 through ../additionalDepreciationAfter1975, which changes nothing because line 26b is floored at zero for a loss on either reading. THE ZERO ANSWER IS THE COMMON ONE AND IS STILL AN ANSWER. The form's own line-26 header says "If straight line depreciation was used, enter -0- on line 26g, except for a corporation subject to section 291", and the instructions say section 1250 recapture "does not apply to dispositions of the following MACRS property placed in service after 1986 ... You are not required to calculate additional depreciation for these properties on line 26", listing 27.5-year residential rental and 22-/31.5-/39-year nonresidential real property. That is the bulk of the TY2025 population and its line 26a is $0 - but $0 ON THE FILER'S OWN STATEMENT, which is what the guard requires rather than assumes. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): an excess is never negative, and the instructions' own line-26d rule ("Do not enter less than zero") carries the same floor for the pre-1976 sibling line. The engine does not enforce a writable's Limit while resolving a dependent fact, so the alias repeats this rule with an explicit GreaterOf floor.

Fact.Name: Section 1254 expenditures and depletion deducted rather than capitalized (Form 4797 Part III line 28a)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 28a, "Intangible drilling and development costs, expenditures for development of mines and other natural deposits, mining exploration costs, and depletion." A FILER CARRY-IN, for the same reason line 26a is one: it is a cumulative history of deductions taken in EARLIER years, and gives this graph no prior-year state to reconstruct it from. ../depreciationAllowed is the line 22 allowed-or-allowable total and is not the same quantity - a mineral property's line 22 depletion is one COMPONENT of line 28a, and the section 263/616/617 expenditures that never entered basis at all are the rest. THIS FACT IS THE POST-1986 QUESTION AND ONLY THAT. It is read where ../propertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987 is FALSE or unanswered; where that Boolean is TRUE the line is ../writableSection1254ExpensesPre1987 instead, and ../section1254Expenses is the fork that chooses. What this fact asks for is the AFTER-1986 list: "the total expenses that" were "deducted under section 263, 616, or 617 by the taxpayer or any other person", "But for such deduction, would have been included in the basis of the property", "plus" "The deduction under section 611 that reduced the adjusted basis of such property". WHAT GOES ON THE LINE DEPENDS ON THE PLACED-IN-THE APPLICATION ERA, and this graph applies the fork: the pre-1987 list is section 263(c) intangible drilling costs ALONE and excludes both the section 616/617 mining deductions and the section 611 depletion the post-1986 list adds, so it is strictly narrower on the same property. Pub. L. 99-514 section 413(c)(1) applies the amended section only to property placed in service after December 31, 1986. NOT CAPPED HERE. Line 28b applies its own minimum against line 24, so line 28a itself is free to exceed the gain; the cap that matters is on the recapture, not on the input - the ../writableAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975 posture verbatim. OPTIONAL (three-state), and the unanswered direction is NOT a silent zero. On an item whose line 24 is a GAIN and whose era is FALSE or unanswered, unanswered REFUSES through ../hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain; on a loss or a zero-gain item it reads as $0 through ../section1254Expenses, which changes nothing because line 28b's minimum is taken against a line 24 floored at zero. WHERE THE ERA IS TRUE THIS FACT IS NOT READ AT ALL and its unansweredness is not refused - the guard tests ../writableSection1254ExpensesPre1987 instead. That is the point of the widening: a pre-1987 filer who answers the pre-1987 question must not be refused for leaving THIS one blank. NO PRINTED ZERO GROUND EXISTS FOR THIS LINE, unlike line 26a's straight-line "-0-" header, which makes the guard MORE clearly right here than there: a property is section 1254 property precisely because such expenditures were deducted, so an attested class with a zero line 28a is the unusual case rather than the bulk of the population. WHAT THIS LINE DOES NOT MODEL, named because the instructions name it: "If you disposed of a portion of section 1254 property or an undivided interest in it, see section 1254(a)(2)" - the partial-disposition allocation. This intake takes the figure the filer computed; it does not perform that allocation. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): an aggregate of deductions taken is never negative, and IRC 1254(a)(1)(A) is an "aggregate amount of" expenditures and depletion deductions. The engine does not enforce a writable's Limit while resolving a dependent fact, so the complete-safe alias repeats this floor explicitly.

Fact.Name: Was this property placed in service before 1987?
Fact.Description: THE FORK THE 2025 INSTRUCTIONS FOR FORM 4797 PUT ON LINE 28a, built here on the SALE collection on 2026-08-31. It is the sale-side twin of form4684:/casualtyEvents/*/writableCasualtyPropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987, which forked the same question on the CASUALTY side on 2026-08-25 and named this collection as the whole of its remaining residual. Line 28a is not one question but two, chosen by the property's placed-in-service date. Property placed in service BEFORE 1987 enters "the total expenses after 1975 that" were "deducted by the taxpayer or any other person as intangible drilling and development costs under section 263(c) (except previously expensed mining costs that were included in income upon reaching the producing state)" and "Would have been reflected in the adjusted basis of the property if they had not been deducted". Property placed in service AFTER 1986 enters the section 263, 616 or 617 deductions PLUS "The deduction under section 611 that reduced the adjusted basis of such property." THE STATUTE DRAWS THE SAME LINE AND IT IS ON DISK, which is what makes this fork more than an instruction-only reading. IRC 1254 as it stands today is the POST-1986 text: the Tax Reform Act of 1986 amended the section generally, and its own transition rule provides that "The amendments made by this section ... shall apply to any disposition of property which is placed in service by the taxpayer after December 31, 1986." Property placed in service before 1987 is therefore governed by FORMER section 1254, whose recapture base is the narrower one the pre-1987 leg prints. Asking the post-1986 question on a pre-1987 disposition recaptures amounts the statute as amended does not reach. WHY IT IS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A SCREEN NOTE: the earlier definition EXCLUDES depletion and mining-exploration costs, and line 28b is a MINIMUM against line 24, so an over-stated 28a can only RAISE the ordinary recapture. That is the taxpayer-ADVERSE direction the era-fork finding named, and it is why this costs an intake rather than a wording change. THE PRINTED DEEMING RULE IS PART OF THIS QUESTION, not a second intake: "Property placed in service after 1986 and acquired under a written contract entered into before September 26, 1985, and binding at all times thereafter is treated as placed in service before 1987." A filer in that position answers YES here. THAT SENTENCE IS ALSO STATUTORY - the same 1986 transition rule carries it as an "Exception for binding contracts" in the same words - so the screen wording rests on primary law, not on the instruction alone. WHAT THE SAME INSTRUCTION SAYS AND THIS BUILD DOES NOT ACT ON, named rather than left silent: i4797 "Line 28" also tells a pre-1987 filer to "Include on Form 4797, line 22, any depletion allowed (or allowable) in determining the adjusted basis of the property". ON THE SALE SIDE LINE 22 IS ../depreciationAllowed AND IT IS ALREADY THE RIGHT LINE - its printed caption is "Depreciation (or depletion) allowed or allowable", so the sentence tells the filer WHAT BELONGS in a figure this collection already collects and feeds through ../adjustedBasis into ../totalGain. It asks for no arithmetic this fork could add, and it is NOT the reason the casualty twin gave (there a section-1254-only event reaches no consumer of line 22 at all). The i4797 "Note" on integrated oil companies completing line 28a by treating section 291(b)(2) amortization as section 263(c) deductions is CORPORATIONS ONLY and cannot arise on a Form 1040 return. NAMED GENERICALLY ON PURPOSE. The placed-in-service era is a property fact, not a section 1254 fact - IRC 1250's own rules turn on it too - so this Boolean is not called ...Section1254PlacedInService... . ONLY THE SECTION 1254 FORK READS IT TODAY, through ../propertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987. SCOPED at the E5 landing (the review's M-3): the STORED VALUE folds in section 413(c)(2)'s binding-contract deeming, which is scoped to that section's own amendments (sections 1254 and 617) and deems NOTHING for section 1250/168 - so a later line-26 build under a different transition regime must ask its own question rather than reuse this one; the generic name reserves the vocabulary, not the answer. The deeming rides on the screen wording, which is load-bearing for the era fork's closure: until it lands, a binding-contract filer answering the bare printed question literally answers NO and takes the adverse post-1986 list. UNANSWERED IS "PLACED IN THE APPLICATION AFTER 1986" through ../propertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987, which is byte-for-byte the behaviour this module had before this change. THE ADVERSE DIRECTION IS REVERSED FOR THE POPULATION THAT ANSWERS AND UNCHANGED FOR THE POPULATION THAT DOES NOT. The filer who never answers is a separate residual, named as such and not closed here. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this disposition exactly where it was before this change.

Fact.Name: Intangible drilling and development costs deducted under section 263(c) after 1975 on this pre-1987 property (Form 4797 Part III line 28a, pre-1987 leg)
Fact.Description: FORM 4797 PART III LINE 28a, THE PRE-1987 LEG, for a SALE or exchange. Read only where BOTH ../isSection1254Property and ../writablePropertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987 are answered true. The sale-side twin of form4684:/casualtyEvents/*/writableCasualtySection1254ExpensesPre1987. IT IS A NARROWER FIGURE THAN ITS POST-1986 SIBLING, and that difference is the whole reason this intake exists: it is section 263(c) intangible drilling and development costs ALONE, excluding previously expensed mining costs that were included in income on reaching the producing state, and excluding BOTH the section 616/617 mining deductions AND the section 611 depletion that ../writableSection1254Expenses asks for. A filer who answered the post-1986 question for pre-1987 property therefore over-stated line 28a, and because line 28b is a minimum against line 24 that could only raise the ordinary recapture - the taxpayer-adverse direction the era-fork finding named. A FILER CARRY-IN, for the same reason its sibling and line 26a are: it is a cumulative history of deductions taken in EARLIER years, and gives this graph no prior-year state to reconstruct it from. NOT CAPPED HERE, exactly as its sibling is not: ../section1254OrdinaryRecaptureContribution applies line 28b's own minimum against the gain, so this input is free to exceed it. THE UNANSWERED DIRECTION IS A REFUSAL, NOT A ZERO, AND THIS IS WHERE THE SALE SIDE PARTS COMPANY WITH THE CASUALTY SIDE. There the pre-1987 figure defaults to $0 and nothing recaptures, which was tolerable only because /knockoutCasualtyGain refuses every return carrying a Section B casualty gain, so no filer reaches it. This collection is LIVE. A silent $0 here would give zero section 1254 ordinary recapture and send the entire gain to Part I, where it can become long-term capital gain - the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE error ../hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain exists to refuse. That guard was widened on 2026-08-31 to test THIS writable on a pre-1987 item, so an attested pre-1987 section 1254 GAIN that leaves this blank REFUSES exactly as its post-1986 sibling does. On a LOSS or a zero-gain item it reads $0 through ../section1254ExpensesPre1987 and changes nothing, because line 28b's minimum is taken against a line 24 floored at zero. WHAT THIS LINE DOES NOT MODEL, named because the instructions name it and because it applies to both legs alike: "If you disposed of a portion of section 1254 property or an undivided interest in it, see section 1254(a)(2)" - the partial-disposition allocation. This intake takes the figure the filer computed; it does not perform that allocation. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): an aggregate of deductions taken is never negative. The engine does not enforce a writable's Limit while resolving a dependent fact, so the complete-safe alias repeats this floor explicitly. It must never be shown on the same disposition as ../writableSection1254Expenses. OPTIONAL: unanswered leaves this disposition exactly where it was before this change, because nothing reaches this fact until the era Boolean is answered true.

Fact.Name: Soil, water, and land clearing expenses deducted on this farm land (Form 4797 Part III line 27a)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 27a, "Soil, water, and land clearing expenses." A FILER CARRY-IN, for the same reason lines 26a and 28a are: it is a cumulative history of deductions taken in EARLIER years, and gives this graph no prior-year state to reconstruct it from. ../depreciationAllowed is the line 22 allowed-or-allowable total and is a different quantity entirely - bare farm land is not depreciable, and section 175 expenditures never entered its basis at all. WHAT THE STATUTE NOW COVERS IS NARROWER THAN THE PRINTED CAPTION, and the gap is named here rather than left to a reader. IRC 1252(a)(1)(A) reads "the aggregate of the deductions allowed under section 175 (relating to soil and water conservation expenditures)" - section 175 ONLY. The land-clearing half was section 182, and Pub. L. 115-141 section 401(b)(32)(B) struck the "and 182 (as in effect on the day before the date of the enactment of the Tax Reform Act of 1986)" clause from (a)(1)(A) in 2018, as it struck "or 182 (relating to expenditures by farmers for clearing land)" from the (a)(2) definition. Section 182 itself was repealed by the 1986 Act. The printed line 27a caption still says "land clearing", and it is vestigial: a section 182 deduction cannot have been allowed within a holding period short enough for this section to apply. This intake is labelled with the printed caption because that is what the filer reads on the form, and it means the section 175 aggregate. NOT CAPPED HERE. Line 27b multiplies it and line 27c applies the only cap the form draws, against line 24. OPTIONAL (three-state), and the unanswered direction is NOT a silent zero inside the percentage bands. On an item whose line 24 is a GAIN and whose ../farmlandFullYearsHeld is under 9, unanswered REFUSES through ../hasUnansweredSection1252ExpensesGain; on a loss, a zero-gain item, or a disposition in the tenth or later year, it reads as $0 through ../section1252Expenses and changes nothing. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): an aggregate of deductions allowed is never negative, and IRC 1252(a)(1)(A) is an "aggregate of the deductions allowed".

Fact.Name: Full years the farm land was held after acquisition (the IRC 1252(a)(3) applicable-percentage driver)
Fact.Description: How many WHOLE YEARS elapsed between the date the farm land was acquired and the date it was disposed of. The driver of IRC 1252(a)(3)'s applicable percentage, which ../section1252Line27b multiplies line 27a by. A THIRD HOLDING-PERIOD INTAKE beside ../heldMoreThanOneYear and ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths, and for the same reason the second one exists: the three ask different questions and none answers another. ../heldMoreThanOneYear is the general section 1231 more-than-one-year test; ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths is section 1231(b)(3)'s 24-month / 12-month count; this is the 5-to-10-year band the section 1252 percentage table is written in. A Boolean at one year expresses none of them. WHY FULL YEARS AND NOT MONTHS. The table's bands break on exact anniversaries - "Within 5 years after the date it was acquired", "Within the sixth year after it was acquired" - so the full-year count lands each band exactly, with no year-or-part rounding to disclose: 0 through 4 full years is "within 5 years", 5 full years is "within the sixth year", and so on. This is the one place in Part III where a whole-year count is EXACT rather than an approximation. (Its section 1255 sibling would not be: IRC 1255(a)(3) counts "each year or part thereof", which is why that class's percentage is the filer's and not this graph's.) UNANSWERED: with both Part III line 19 dates entered, the count is taken from the dates (../farmlandFullYearsByDates; the anniversary day belongs to the earlier band); with the dates not both entered, a GAIN takes no default - line 27b and every total it feeds stay Incomplete until the count is answered (../farmlandFullYearsHeld), and a gain whose line 27a is also unanswered is still refused (../hasUnansweredSection1252ExpensesGain). On a loss or zero gain the count cannot move a number and is not needed. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): a holding period is not negative. ONLY MEANINGFUL on an item whose ../isSection1252Property is answered TRUE.

Fact.Name: Applicable percentage of the section 126 payments excluded from income (Form 4797 Part III line 29a)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 29a, "Applicable percentage of payments excluded from income under section 126." A FILER CARRY-IN, and note WHAT is carried in: the printed line asks for the PRODUCT - the applicable percentage already applied to the excluded payments - not the raw payments. That is why this class needs one intake where section 1252 needs two, and why there is no line 29c: line 29b is the minimum against line 24 and the block ends. THE PERCENTAGE THE FILER APPLIES is IRC 1255(a)(3): 100 percent for a disposition less than 10 years after the section 126 payments were received, and thereafter "100 percent reduced (but not below zero) by 10 percent for each year or part thereof in excess of 10 years such property was held after the date of receipt of the payments". The instructions print the same rule in the same order and add the far end explicitly: "Use zero if 20 years or more." WHY IT IS NOT COMPUTED HERE, stated as a disclosed limit rather than left implicit. Two reasons, and the first alone is sufficient: the printed line asks for one number, so a graph that asked for the payments and the receipt date would be asking the filer for something the form does not. The second is that the statute counts "each year or part thereof", which a whole-year intake cannot express exactly at an anniversary and a month intake could only approximate against a receipt date this collection does not carry. The section 1252 twin is different in both respects - the form prints the multiplication as its own line 27b, and every band of IRC 1252(a)(3) breaks on an exact anniversary - which is why THAT percentage IS computed here, on ../section1252Line27b. NOT CAPPED HERE. OPTIONAL (three-state), and the unanswered direction is NOT a silent zero: on an item whose line 24 is a GAIN, unanswered REFUSES through ../hasUnansweredSection1255PaymentsGain; on a loss or a zero-gain item it reads as $0 through ../section1255ApplicablePercentageOfPayments, which changes nothing because line 29b's minimum is taken against a line 24 floored at zero. NON-NEGATIVE (declared Limit): a percentage of an aggregate of excluded payments is never negative.

Fact.Description: ../isSection1255Property when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1254PropertyComplete idiom verbatim).
