Fact.Name: Full years the farm land was held (answered, else from the line 19 dates, else unresolved on a gain)
Fact.Description: The IRC 1252(a)(3) band index. Three sources, in order: ../writableFarmlandFullYearsHeld when answered, floored at 0; else, with both Part III line 19 dates entered, ../farmlandFullYearsByDates; else, when line 24 is not a gain, 0 - line 27c is the smaller of line 24 and line 27b, floored at 0, so no band can move a number and the count is not needed. Otherwise (a GAIN with the count unknown) no case matches and this fact is Incomplete, and so are line 27b and every total it feeds: the return waits for the answer. There is no 100 percent default any more. READ TWICE: by ../section1252Line27b for the band, and by ../hasUnansweredSection1252ExpensesGain, which stands down only on a KNOWN count of 9 or more (the instructions say to skip line 27 there); an unknown count keeps that refusal in force, so a gain with both line 27a and the count unanswered still refuses. Neither reader is reached for a disposition that is not attested section 1252 farm land.

Fact.Name: Livestock carve-out attestation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../isLivestock when answered. UNANSWERED, it is false only where the answer cannot change this item's routing - the item is not attested section 1245 personalty (livestock is section 1245 property; no other class asks the question), it is property IRC 1231(b)(1) excludes or de minimis property (Part II whatever the holding period), it is a LOSS (the not-livestock reading keeps it in the section 1231 netting, the adverse direction for a loss), or both Part III line 19 dates are entered and show it held under 12 months (every holding test fails) or 24 months or more (every test passes). Anywhere else - a gain whose holding period could fall from the 12-month anniversary up to the 24-month anniversary, where IRC 1231(b)(3) and the more-than-one-year test disagree - no case matches and this fact is Incomplete, and so is the item's routing: the return waits for the answer. The dates cannot answer a property-class question; they can only show it does not matter. True SWITCHES the item onto the section 1231(b)(3) month test: the livestock arm of ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod routes the non-recapture remainder on ../livestockSection1231HoldingMet instead of the more-than-one-year test.

Fact.Name: The 24-month cattle/horse threshold applies to this item (complete-safe, unanswered -> TRUE)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsCattleOrHorses when answered, else TRUE. DELIBERATELY NOT the "else false" direction the ../isLivestockComplete / ../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete wrappers use, and the name says so rather than borrowing the "...Complete" suffix that elsewhere in this module always means "answered else false": here FALSE is the taxpayer-FAVOURABLE reading, so it cannot be the silent default. Reading an unanswered class question as "other livestock" would apply the SHORTER 12-month threshold and could route a 12-to-23-month CATTLE gain into recapture-plus-section-1231 (long-term capital gain on the excess), where chart row 7a routes it to Part II as wholly ordinary income - the precise misroute the holding-period re-derivation opened the livestock refusal to prevent. Reading it as cattle or horses can only WITHHOLD section 1231 treatment from a 12-to-23-month OTHER-livestock item, so the unanswered default never grants a better answer than the taxpayer proves. THE CONSEQUENCE OF WITHHOLDING CHANGED ON 2026-08-03, and the justification has to be re-derived rather than left standing on its old sentence. Until then the withheld item was REFUSED (../isInScope excluded sub-threshold livestock), so "withhold" cost the filer nothing but a refusal. Now the withheld item is ROUTED to Part II as wholly ordinary income, which is a real tax consequence, and the default's safety has to be argued in both directions: FOR A GAIN it still holds, and more strongly than before. Withholding section 1231 treatment turns what might have been a long-term capital excess into ordinary income - taxpayer- ADVERSE, the World-#1 direction. FOR A LOSS IT DOES NOT HOLD AT ALL, and something else carries the load: withholding section 1231 treatment from a loss routes it to Part II ordinary, which BYPASSES the section 1231 netting against answered long-term gains and is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE. That case is refused outright by ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss, which is what makes this default safe in 2026-08-03's graph. Always resolves Complete (an IsComplete Switch with a True tail), so nothing downstream can inherit an Incomplete from an unanswered class question.

Fact.Name: Months the livestock was held (the answered count, floored at 0; unanswered takes no case)
Fact.Description: ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths when answered, floored at 0 (a Min-0 writable is not enforced on resolution). Unanswered, this fact takes no case and is Incomplete - there is no zero default any more. It is read only by ../livestockSection1231HoldingMet, and only behind the writable's own IsComplete; when the count is unanswered that fact takes the section 1231(b)(3) test from both Part III line 19 dates if they are entered, and otherwise stays Incomplete on a GAIN (the return waits for the answer) and reads false on a LOSS, which ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss refuses.

Fact.Name: The section 1231(b)(3) holding threshold in months for this animal (24 or 12)
Fact.Description: 24 months when ../appliesCattleOrHorseThreshold is true (cattle and horses, or an unanswered class question), else 12 months (other livestock). The two numbers are the whole content of IRC section 1231(b)(3)'s split and of the Form 4797 chart's rows 7 and 8; naming the threshold as its own Int keeps ../livestockSection1231HoldingMet a single comparison instead of a nested fork. MEANINGLESS on a non-livestock item, where it resolves 24 and nothing reads it: the routing gate ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod only consults the livestock test for an item whose ../isLivestockComplete is true.

Fact.Name: Livestock met its section 1231 holding period (24 months cattle/horses, 12 months other)
Fact.Description: ../livestockHoldingMonthsComplete is at least ../livestockThresholdMonths. The comparison is INCLUSIVE on both thresholds because the statute is: section 1231(b)(3) says "24 months or MORE" and "12 months or MORE", and the chart's own column headings split at "Held less than 24 months" against "Held 24 months or more". So 24 months exactly PASSES for cattle and 12 months exactly PASSES for other livestock; 23 and 11 fail. WHAT TURNS ON IT. True is the condition on which an attested-livestock disposition's non-recapture remainder is a section 1231 amount rather than Part II ordinary (../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod). FALSE no longer refuses the item: it puts it in ../livestockPartIIOrdinaryRouting's population, which chart rows 7a/7b and 8a/8b send to Part II, and only a LOSS there resting on an unanswered intake still refuses (../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss). THREE SOURCES, in order: the answered month count against the threshold; else, with both Part III line 19 dates entered, ../heldTwentyFourMonthsOrMoreByDates (cattle and horses, or an unanswered class) or ../heldTwelveMonthsOrMoreByDates (other livestock), each counting the anniversary as qualifying; else, on a LOSS, false - the item is refused by ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss and false keeps its section 1231 leg at 0 beside the named refusal. Otherwise (a GAIN with the count unknown) no case matches and this fact is Incomplete: the return waits for the answer. Its readers never feed an Incomplete from it into ../isInScope: ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod reads it only on the livestock arm, and ../livestockPartIIOrdinaryRouting is read by the refusal behind an IsComplete guard.

Fact.Name: Held more than one year (the attestation, else derived from the line 19 dates, else unresolved)
Fact.Description: The general more-than-one-year holding test this item routes on. Three sources, in order: (1) ../heldMoreThanOneYear when the filer answered it; (2) otherwise, when BOTH Part III line 19 date columns are entered (../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired and ../writableLineNineteenDateSold), the holding period those dates show (../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates, the IRC 1231(b)(1) and 1222 "more than 1 year" rule counted from the day after acquisition through the day of sale); (3) for a LOSS in that position, false: the item is refused by ../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss, and false keeps its components at 0 so the section 1231 totals stay legible beside the named refusal (the value can reach no filed return); (4) otherwise NOTHING - the Switch has no default case and runs off the end, so this fact is Incomplete and so is the routing of the item's non-recapture remainder (../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod, ../routesToSection1231, ../section1231Component, ../partIIOrdinaryComponent) and every total they feed. The return does not complete until the filer answers the question or enters both dates. WHY NO DEFAULT. The chart routes a gain on depreciable business property to Part II when "Held 1 year or less" and to Part III (1245) when "Held more than 1 year"; it prints no third branch, and the holding period is always knowable by the filer from the dates it counts. Reading an unanswered holding period as one year or less would silently tax a long-held gain's section 1231 excess at ordinary rates; reading it as more than one year would silently grant section 1231 treatment the filer never showed. Neither is a reading of the form, so neither is taken. NOT READ ON A LIVESTOCK ITEM'S ROUTING (the month test replaces it there), and NOT READ on an item IRC 1231(b)(1) excludes or on de minimis safe-harbor property: ../routesToSection1231 is an All whose excluded or expensed conjunct is Complete false, which decides the All without this fact, so such an item's remainder is Part II ordinary whether or not the holding period is known. A LOSS whose holding period is neither answered nor dated is still refused (../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss, case 3), because the refusal names the missing input on the screen rather than leaving an unexplained Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Item cleared the holding period its own property class uses (section 1231 vs Part II routing)
Fact.Description: THE HOLDING-PERIOD HALF of the routing gate for the non-recapture remainder: ../routesToSection1231 reads it beside the two section 1231 qualification questions, and true there sends the remainder to Form 4797 Part I as a section 1231 amount (../section1231Component), false to Part II as ordinary (../partIIOrdinaryComponent). It exists because the graph now holds TWO holding tests and each property class uses exactly one of them - an attested-livestock item uses the section 1231(b)(3) month test (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet), every other item uses the general more-than-one-year test (../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete), which is what those two components read individually before this fact existed. IT MOVES NOTHING FOR A NON-LIVESTOCK ITEM, by construction rather than by measurement: the Switch's default arm IS ../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete, so for every disposition whose ../isLivestockComplete is false this fact is that Boolean, unchanged, and every committed non-livestock Form 4797 case resolves byte-identically. WHAT IT DECIDES FOR THE SUB-THRESHOLD LIVESTOCK POPULATION. That population used to be refused upstream, so this gate's FALSE verdict only chose which leg carried a Result.Incomplete. The section 1231 aggregates resolve Complete-0 for such an item, as they did before, but now on a return that FILES rather than one that refuses. WHY THE TWO TESTS CANNOT BE COLLAPSED, restated where the routing happens: they disagree in BOTH directions. Cattle held 18 months is "more than 1 year" but has not met 24 months (chart row 7a routes that gain to Part II as wholly ordinary income - the holding-period re-derivation's misroute). Other livestock held exactly 12 months HAS met section 1231(b)(3)(B) but is not "more than 1 year", because a holding period runs from the day after acquisition; chart row 8a routes that gain to Part III and its excess to Part I, so reading heldMoreThanOneYear there would strand a genuine section 1231 amount in Part II. Incomplete - the intended block, not a default - while the question that decides it is unanswered and the dates cannot decide it: ../isLivestockComplete itself (an unanswered livestock question in the 12-to-24-month window), the livestock month test (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet), or the general test (../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete). Both arms are guarded (the second reads Not(../isLivestockComplete)), so an undecided class runs off the end rather than taking the general arm as a Placeholder.

Fact.Name: Property is excluded from section 1231 by IRC 1231(b)(1)(A)-(D) (inventory, property held for sale to customers, self-created creative property, U.S. Government publications)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Is this property any of the following: inventory, or property you held primarily for sale to customers; a patent, invention, model or design, secret formula or process, copyright, or literary, musical or artistic composition, letter or memorandum, or similar property, created by your own efforts, prepared or produced for you (letters, memoranda or similar property), or received from its creator in a way that gave you the creator's basis (such as by gift); or a U.S. Government publication you received from the government other than by purchase at the price offered to the public, or received from someone who had received it that way, in a way that gave you their basis (such as by gift)?" HELP TEXT: "Section 1231 treatment - where a net gain can be taxed as a long-term capital gain - is only for property used in your trade or business, and the law excludes these kinds of property from it. Their sale produces ordinary income, reported in Part II of Form 4797, however long you held them. Answer No for ordinary business equipment, vehicles, buildings and purchased intangibles." SOURCES: IRC 1231(b)(1)(A)-(D) (26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024, right column); the Instructions for Form 4797, "Transactions to which section 1231 does not apply" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 6, left column, continuing as the bullets at lines 358-377, right column - the prepared-or-produced leg at lines 364-365 and the carryover-basis leg for publications at lines 374-377); Pub 544 on property for sale to customers and on patents and copyrights (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p544.pdf, page 41, left column). ASKED WHEN: every Part III disposition that attests a printed class. UNANSWERED: read as NOT excluded (../isSection1231ExcludedPropertyComplete false), so the item routes exactly as it did before this question existed. This is the complete-safe additivity this collection already applies to a newly added optional carve-out question (see ../isLivestock): every already-attested return keeps resolving. DISCLOSED LIMIT: a genuinely excluded item whose owner never answers still computes its non-recapture remainder as a section 1231 amount - long-term capital gain rates on what the law makes ordinary income - so the application should put the question on every Part III item rather than leave it skippable in practice. VALIDATION: Boolean, Yes / No, no default, no Min or Max. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../isSection1231ExcludedPropertyComplete, hence ../routesToSection1231: YES sends the item's non-recapture remainder to Part II as ordinary income (../partIIOrdinaryComponent) whatever its holding period, and takes it out of Part I line 6, line 7 and the unrecaptured section 1250 gain group. The recapture on lines 25b through 29b is unchanged.

Fact.Name: Property's cost was deducted under the de minimis safe harbor for tangible property
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Did you deduct this property's cost under the de minimis safe harbor for tangible property instead of depreciating it?" HELP TEXT: "The de minimis safe harbor lets a business deduct the cost of a low-cost item in the year it is bought (currently $2,500 or less, or $5,000 or less if you have an applicable financial statement). If you did that for this property, it is not section 1231 property when you sell it: any gain is ordinary income, reported on line 10 of Form 4797, however long you held it." SOURCES: Pub 544 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p544.pdf, page 41, left column), whose worked example deducts a $1,000 machine under the safe harbor and sells it for $1,500: "you must report the $1,500 as ordinary gain on line 10 of Form 4797"; the Instructions for Form 4797, Line 10 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 8, left column) and the "Where To Make First Entry" chart, row 4, which sends such property to Part II in BOTH holding-period columns (lines 40-42). The Treasury regulation that defines the safe harbor is not vendored here, so the thresholds in the help text are Pub 544's own. ASKED WHEN: every Part III disposition that attests a printed class. UNANSWERED: read as NO (../wasDeductedUnderDeMinimisSafeHarborComplete false) - the same complete-safe additivity as ../writableIsSection1231ExcludedProperty and ../isLivestock. DISCLOSED LIMIT: an expensed item whose owner never answers still computes its gain as a section 1231 amount. VALIDATION: Boolean, Yes / No, no default, no Min or Max. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../wasDeductedUnderDeMinimisSafeHarborComplete, hence ../routesToSection1231: YES CHARACTERISES the item's non-recapture remainder as Part II ordinary income; the recapture is untouched. An expensed item carries $0 in column (e), so its line 25b is $0 and its whole gain is the remainder - Pub 544's $1,500.

Fact.Name: Section 1231(b)(1) exclusion attestation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsSection1231ExcludedProperty when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1250PropertyComplete idiom). Unanswered reads as not excluded, which keeps the question ADDITIVE: an item that answered its class before this question existed routes exactly as it did. The favourable direction of that default is disclosed on the writable.

Fact.Name: De minimis safe harbor attestation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableWasDeductedUnderDeMinimisSafeHarbor when answered, else false (the IsComplete pattern, the ../isSection1250PropertyComplete idiom). Unanswered reads as NO, which keeps the question ADDITIVE; the favourable direction of that default is disclosed on the writable.

Fact.Name: Item's non-recapture remainder is a section 1231 amount (holding period met, not excluded by IRC 1231(b)(1), not de minimis safe-harbor property)
Fact.Description: THE ROUTING GATE for the non-recapture remainder: true sends it to Form 4797 Part I as a section 1231 amount (../section1231Component), false sends it to Part II as ordinary (../partIIOrdinaryComponent), and ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent reads it as the worksheet's "for which you made an entry in Part I" clause. THREE conjuncts: the item cleared the holding period its own class uses (../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod - the general more-than-one-year test, or the livestock month test); it is NOT property IRC 1231(b)(1)(A)-(D) excludes (../isSection1231ExcludedPropertyComplete); and its cost was NOT deducted under the de minimis safe harbor (../wasDeductedUnderDeMinimisSafeHarborComplete), which Pub 544 and chart row 4 send to Part II whatever the holding period. An excluded or expensed item's remainder is therefore ordinary however long it was held, and no section 1231 gain is left in it to be unrecaptured. THE RECAPTURE IS NOT TOUCHED: lines 25b through 29b compute as before; the two questions CHARACTERISE the remainder, they do not change it. IT MOVES NOTHING WHERE BOTH QUESTIONS ARE UNANSWERED OR ANSWERED NO: the gate is then ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod unchanged, so no committed case moves. Complete whenever the holding period is known; Incomplete when it is not, EXCEPT on an item answered excluded or de minimis, where the Complete-false conjunct decides the All on its own.

Fact.Name: Adjusted basis (Form 4797 Part III line 23)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 23 = line 21 minus line 22 (cost or other basis minus depreciation allowed). The property's adjusted basis at the time of disposition.

Fact.Name: Total gain (Form 4797 Part III line 24)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 24 = line 20 minus line 23 (gross sales price minus adjusted basis) = the total gain realized on the disposition. May be zero or negative (a section 1231 / Part II loss). NOT floored here so the sign drives the recapture and remainder split.

Fact.Name: Unanswered holding period on a loss disposition (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: True when the item's holding period is UNKNOWN - ../heldMoreThanOneYear is unanswered AND the two Part III line 19 date columns are not both entered, so ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates cannot answer it either - and the item's total gain (line 24) is NEGATIVE (a loss; recapture is 0 on a loss, so the non-recapture remainder is the whole negative total gain). Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. The refusal, rather than the bare Incomplete an unknown-holding GAIN resolves to (../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete), is kept for the loss because it names the missing input: a loss with no holding period can neither be netted in section 1231 nor deducted in Part II, and the filer is told so. COMPLETE-SAFETY: this gate depends only on the item's OWN raw writables (the completeness of the attestation and of the two dates; totalGain is pure per-item arithmetic over grossSalesPrice / costOrOtherBasis / depreciationAllowed) - never a flow-derived fact - so it can never cascade Placeholder/Incomplete into a return without this item. When either ../isSection1231ExcludedPropertyComplete or ../wasDeductedUnderDeMinimisSafeHarborComplete is affirmatively true this refusal is suppressed, because ../routesToSection1231 sends the remainder to Part II regardless of holding period; without either affirmative answer the guard remains in force.

Fact.Name: Sub-threshold livestock: routes to Part II ordinary (Form 4797 chart rows 7a/7b, 8a/8b)
Fact.Description: True for an attested-livestock item that has NOT met its section 1231(b)(3) holding threshold — the population Form 4797's "Where To Make First Entry" chart sends to Part II. Rows 7a and 7b send cattle and horses "Held less than 24 months" to Part II whether sold at a gain or at a loss, and rows 8a and 8b do the same for other livestock held less than 12 months. IT NAMES A POPULATION; IT IS NOT A GATE. Before 2026-08-03 this population was REFUSED by ../isInScope, and the build that admitted it did NOT do so by adding an arm that reads this fact — it REMOVED the livestock arm entirely, because once sub-threshold livestock is admitted the arm's condition is unconditionally true. What reads this fact is ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss, whose first conjunct is exactly "this item is in the newly-admitted population"; naming it here keeps that guard a single readable All and puts the routing verdict in the snapshot, where a reader can see WHY an item's remainder went to Part II rather than Part I. WHAT IT DOES NOT DECIDE. The routing itself is ../routesToSection1231, whose holding-period half ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriod was already false for this population; that gate is what ../partIIOrdinaryComponent reads. This fact adds no arithmetic; it re-states, at a name, the condition under which that routing applies to livestock. RAISED VERSUS PURCHASED IS INERT IN THIS POPULATION, which is worth stating where the population is named because it is stronger here than the general argument on ../isLivestock. Rows 7c and 8c differ from 7a and 8a only in the "Held 24 (or 12) months or more" column, where the raised animal goes to Part I and the purchased one to Part III. In the "Held less than" column - the whole of this population - all six rows read Part II. There is nothing for a raised-versus-purchased attestation to decide about an item this fact is true for. TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Boolean; no rounding. Complete-FALSE on every non-livestock item (the All short-circuits on ../isLivestockComplete). Incomplete on an attested-livestock item whose month count is neither answered nor dated; its only consumer, ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss, reads it behind an IsComplete guard, so the Incomplete never reaches ../isInScope.

Fact.Name: Unanswered livestock input on a sub-threshold livestock LOSS (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: The livestock twin of ../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss, and the price of admitting the sub-threshold population. True when the item is attested livestock, its total gain (line 24) is NEGATIVE, it is not excluded or de minimis property, and EITHER its month count is unknown - ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths unanswered AND the two Part III line 19 dates not both entered, so ../livestockSection1231HoldingMet cannot take the test from the dates either - OR its class question ../writableIsCattleOrHorses is unanswered and the item is sub-threshold under the 24-month reading that fills it (../livestockPartIIOrdinaryRouting, read behind its IsComplete). Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. With both dates entered the month count is known and only the class half can refuse. WHY A LOSS AND NOT A GAIN. Routing a sub-threshold livestock LOSS to Part II ordinary BYPASSES the section 1231 netting against answered long-term gains — the loss deducts at ordinary rates while the untouched gain keeps long-term rates, taxpayer-FAVOURABLE whenever they coexist — and it suppresses the section 1231(c) lookback entry. That is fine when the inputs are answered and the item is genuinely sub-threshold, because then the chart really does say Part II (rows 7b and 8b). It is not fine when the sub-threshold verdict rests on an input nobody stated. A GAIN needs no such guard: the sub-threshold routing makes the whole gain ordinary, which is the conservative direction, so the module keeps its usual answer-blind default there - superseded for an UNKNOWN month count, which now leaves a gain Incomplete (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet) rather than defaulting it to Part II. WHY BOTH INTAKES AND NOT JUST THE MONTH COUNT. An unknown month count cannot be routed at all, so it refuses on its own. DELIBERATELY OVER-REFUSING, AND BY HOW MUCH. An unanswered class on an item held under 12 months is decided by neither reading — both thresholds fail — so this gate refuses a return it could in principle route. The precise version would compare the month count against the 12-month floor, which means a second copy of the statute's constant and a fork no printed source draws. The whole over-refused population REFUSED BEFORE THIS CHANGE, so the imprecision takes nothing away from anyone - it only declines to hand back something the dictionary was under no obligation to hand back - and it is the conservative direction. Rejected alternative: guard the month count only, which leaves the class half of the hazard open. COMPLETE-SAFETY: like its twin, this gate reads only the item's OWN raw writables (two completeness tests, plus ../totalGain, which is pure per-item arithmetic) and ../livestockPartIIOrdinaryRouting, itself two complete-safe wrappers — never a flow-derived fact — so it can never cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item (the cascade lesson). Complete-false on every committed scenario, none of which attests livestock. the owner ruling: an affirmative section 1231 exclusion or de minimis answer suppresses this livestock-input refusal too, because the remainder is already ordinary regardless of holding period or livestock threshold; with neither affirmative answer, the existing guard remains in force. The ruling's fixture is the first committed scenario that attests livestock; the preceding sentence describes the earlier fixture set.

Fact.Name: Unanswered line 26a on a section 1250 GAIN (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: The THIRD sibling of ../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss and ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss, and the price of admitting the section 1250 class. True when the item is attested section 1250 real property, its total gain (line 24) is POSITIVE, and ../writableAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975 is UNANSWERED. Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. THE DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE REASON IT EXISTS. Unanswered-is-zero would give zero section 1250 ordinary recapture and send the entire gain to Part I, where it can become long-term capital gain - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so it cannot be a silent default. This is the ../isSection1245Property posture (an unanswered class question refuses), not the ../isLivestock one (an unanswered categorical carve-out leaves the item in scope). THE PRINTED ZERO IS REAL AND IS NOT THE SAME THING, which is the objection this paragraph exists to answer. The form's own line-26 header says "If straight line depreciation was used, enter -0- on line 26g, except for a corporation subject to section 291", and the instructions say section 1250 recapture "does not apply to dispositions of the following MACRS property placed in service after 1986 ... You are not required to calculate additional depreciation for these properties on line 26", listing 27.5-year residential rental and 22-/31.5-/39-year nonresidential real property. A LOSS NEEDS NO GUARD, and the arithmetic says so rather than a judgement: line 26b is the applicable percentage multiplied by the SMALLER of line 24 and line 26a, with line 24 floored at zero, so line 26g is 0 for a loss item whatever line 26a holds. COMPLETE-SAFETY, stated because both sibling guards state it and the cascade lesson is what it protects: this gate reads only the item's OWN raw writables - one completeness test on ../writableAdditionalDepreciationAfter1975, one wrapper over ../isSection1250Property, and ../totalGain, which is pure per-item arithmetic over ../grossSalesPrice, ../costOrOtherBasis and ../depreciationAllowed - and never a flow-derived fact, so it cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item. Complete-FALSE on every return that reports no section 1250 disposition, which is every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: Unanswered line 28a on a section 1254 GAIN (refusal gate)
Fact.Description:
The FOURTH sibling of ../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss, ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss and ../hasUnansweredAdditionalDepreciationGain, and the price of admitting the section 1254 class. True when the item is attested section 1254 property, its total gain (line 24) is POSITIVE, and THE ERA-APPROPRIATE line 28a intake is UNANSWERED - ../writableSection1254ExpensesPre1987 where ../propertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987 is true, ../writableSection1254Expenses otherwise. Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. THE DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE REASON IT EXISTS. Unanswered-is-zero would give zero section 1254 ordinary recapture and send the entire gain to Part I, where it can become long-term capital gain - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so it cannot be a silent default. This is the ../isSection1245Property posture (an unanswered class question refuses), not the ../isLivestock one (an unanswered categorical carve-out leaves the item in scope). THERE IS ONE PRINTED ROUTE TO A REAL ZERO AND IT IS NARROWER THAN LINE 26a's TWO, which is the honest version of a sentence that read "Line 28 prints no such ground at all" until adversarial review corrected it on 2026-08-17. That sentence was FALSE, and it was the load-bearing justification for a new whole-return refusal, so it is corrected here rather than softened. What the instructions actually print: THE ERA FORK IS THE WHOLE POINT. The "must recapture all expenses" clause is written about ONE era, and the first cut of this change quoted it with its subject clipped off. In full: "If you had a gain on the disposition of oil, gas, geothermal, or other mineral properties (section 1254 property) PLACED IN THE APPLICATION AFTER 1986, you must recapture all expenses that were deducted as intangible drilling costs, depletion, mine exploration costs, and development costs under sections 263, 616, and 617." FOR PRE-1987 PROPERTY THE PRINTED LIST IS NARROWER: line 28a is "the total expenses after 1975 that" were "deducted by the taxpayer or any other person as intangible drilling and development costs under section 263(c)" - IDC ONLY, with no section 616/617 mining costs and no section 611 depletion. So a pre-1987 mineral property whose only deducted amounts were mining exploration or development costs has a PRINTED line 28a of zero, and this guard refuses it anyway.
THE ERA FORK IS NOW THIS GRAPH'S TO APPLY, AND THIS GUARD APPLIES IT. The refusal did not weaken and it did not widen - it MOVED to the era-appropriate intake. A pre-1987 item that answers ../writableSection1254ExpensesPre1987 is no longer refused for leaving the post-1986 question blank, which is the whole point of the build: without this change the new intake would be worse than inert, because answering it would earn a refusal. And a pre-1987 item that leaves the pre-1987 intake blank IS refused, for the reason the paragraph above gives and which is unchanged by the fork - a silent $0 sends the entire gain to Part I where it can become long-term capital gain, the taxpayer-favourable error this guard exists to prevent. The filer whose printed pre-1987 line 28a genuinely is zero types the 0 they already derived; that is still one keystroke, and it is now asked about the RIGHT line. The line 26a twin makes the same trade against two printed zero grounds that ARE checkable in principle, so this guard is no weaker than its sibling, just differently argued. THE RESIDUE THIS KEEPS IS THE DATA-COMPLETENESS ONE AND ONLY THAT: an attested section 1254 gain whose own line 28a the filer has not stated, in whichever era the filer attested. That is the correct permanent refusal - two readings of the statute's leg (A) are available and the filer holds the deduction history that picks between them. A LOSS NEEDS NO GUARD, and the arithmetic says so rather than a judgement: line 28b is the smaller of line 28a and line 24 floored at zero, so line 28b is 0 for a loss item whatever line 28a holds. COMPLETE-SAFETY, stated because all three sibling guards state it and the cascade lesson is what it protects: this gate reads only the item's OWN raw writables - one completeness test on each of ../writableSection1254Expenses and ../writableSection1254ExpensesPre1987, two wrappers over the item's own Booleans (../isSection1254Property and ../propertyPlacedInServiceBefore1987, each an IsComplete/Switch that is itself always Complete), and ../totalGain, which is pure per-item arithmetic over ../grossSalesPrice, ../costOrOtherBasis and ../depreciationAllowed - and never a flow-derived fact, so it cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item. NOTE WHICH SIDE THE IsComplete IS ON: the era branch is read through the complete-safe WRAPPER (an IsComplete on the wrapper would be always-true and would test nothing), while the two completeness tests are on the RAW writables, which is the only place they mean anything. Complete-FALSE on every return that reports no section 1254 disposition, which is every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: Section 1254 attested TOGETHER with section 1245 or section 1250 (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: True when the item attests section 1254 AND at least one of the other two classes this module models. Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT A PRECEDENCE, which is what the first cut of the section 1254 build shipped on 2026-08-17 and what adversarial review sent back the same day. The module orders section 1245 BEFORE section 1250 on a PROVEN inequality: line 25b is the smaller of the gain and ALL the depreciation, line 26g is the smaller of the gain and only the EXCESS over straight line, so 25b is never smaller than 26g for the same property and taking the section 1245 arm can only over-recapture. NO SUCH INEQUALITY EXISTS IN EITHER DIRECTION AGAINST LINE 28b, and both failures are concrete rather than theoretical: (1) AGAINST LINE 26g. A section-1250-first precedence therefore reports $0 of ordinary recapture on an item whose line 28b is the ENTIRE GAIN, and sends the whole amount to Part I where it can become long-term capital gain. (2) AGAINST LINE 25b. Line 25a is the line 22 "Depreciation (or depletion) allowed or allowable", which carries the section 611 DEPLETION but NOT the section 263(c) intangible drilling costs or the section 616/617 mining costs - those were deducted and never entered basis at all, which is the whole reason section 1254 exists. So line 25b can be far SMALLER than line 28b, and the section-1245-first precedence is provably conservative only against line 26g. THE PRINTED FORM WOULD ADD THE BLOCKS, NOT ORDER THEM. Line 31 is "Add property columns A through D, lines 25b, 26g, 27c, 28b, and 29b" - one join over every class block the property completes. This module models ONE class per item, so it has no printed warrant for choosing between two attested blocks, and the sum is not available to it either: each block takes its own minimum against line 24, so adding two of them can report more ordinary income than there was gain. A COMPUTED GreaterOf(26g, 28b) WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, because it buys the ordinary line at the price of a second silent error one worksheet away: the Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 2 is printed as "Enter the amount from Form 4797, line 26g, for the property for which you made an entry on line 1", so a return whose ordinary recapture was actually line 28b would measure its 25%-rate slice against a line 26g the return did not use. Refusing keeps the contradiction in one place. SO THIS IS THE CORRECT-REFUSAL CLASS, not a deferral: two of the filer's own attestations name property classes with different recapture rules and no printed order between them, no computation can decide which the filer meant, and the remedy is a corrected answer. It is also a strict NARROWING of a total refusal - before 2026-08-17 every section 1254 item refused, so no return that could file loses anything here. THE OTHER CONTRADICTORY PAIR IS NOT HERE and keeps its precedence: an item attesting both section 1245 and section 1250 still takes the section 1245 arm, on the proven inequality above. Only the pairs involving section 1254 are unordered. COMPLETE-SAFETY: three complete-safe class wrappers and nothing else, so this gate cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item, and it is Complete-FALSE on every committed scenario (none answers ../isSection1254Property).

Fact.Name: Unanswered line 27a on a section 1252 GAIN inside the percentage bands (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: The FIFTH sibling of ../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss, ../hasUnansweredLivestockInputsLoss, ../hasUnansweredAdditionalDepreciationGain and ../hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain, and the price of admitting the section 1252 class. True when the item is attested section 1252 farm land, its total gain (line 24) is POSITIVE, ../writableSection1252Expenses is UNANSWERED, and ../farmlandFullYearsHeld is UNDER 9. Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. THE DIRECTION IS THE REASON IT EXISTS. Unanswered-is-zero would give zero section 1252 ordinary recapture and send the entire gain to Part I, where it can become long-term capital gain - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so it cannot be a silent default. This is the ../hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain posture. THE FOURTH CONJUNCT IS WHAT MAKES THIS GUARD NARROWER THAN ITS SECTION 1254 TWIN, and it is printed rather than reasoned. The instructions say "Skip line 27 if you dispose of such farmland during the 10th or later year after you acquired it", and IRC 1252(a)(3) gives 0 percent from ten years on. At 9 or more full years held, line 27b is zero whatever line 27a holds, so an unanswered line 27a cannot move a number and refusing the return would refuse a filer the instructions excuse from the line altogether. The section 1254 twin has no such band because its era fork is UNKNOWABLE to this graph; here the band is knowable, because ../writableFarmlandFullYearsHeld asks for it. AN UNANSWERED YEAR COUNT DOES NOT ESCAPE THE GUARD: ../farmlandFullYearsHeld reads 0, which is under 9, so an item that answers neither intake still refuses. A LOSS NEEDS NO GUARD, and the arithmetic says so rather than a judgement: line 27c is the smaller of line 27b and line 24 floored at zero, so line 27c is 0 for a loss item whatever line 27a holds. COMPLETE-SAFETY: this gate reads only the item's OWN raw writables - one completeness test on ../writableSection1252Expenses, one wrapper over ../isSection1252Property, one wrapper over ../writableFarmlandFullYearsHeld, and ../totalGain, which is pure per-item arithmetic - and never a flow-derived fact, so it cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item. Complete-FALSE on every return that reports no section 1252 disposition, which is every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: Unanswered line 29a on a section 1255 GAIN (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: The SIXTH sibling of the module's unanswered-input guards, and the price of admitting the section 1255 class. True when the item is attested section 126 cost-sharing property, its total gain (line 24) is POSITIVE, and ../writableSection1255ApplicablePercentageOfPayments is UNANSWERED. Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. THE DIRECTION IS THE REASON IT EXISTS, the ../hasUnansweredSection1254ExpensesGain argument unchanged: unanswered-is-zero would give zero section 1255 ordinary recapture and send the entire gain to Part I, where it can become long-term capital gain - taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, so it cannot be a silent default. NO PRINTED STAND-DOWN BAND, unlike the section 1252 twin. IRC 1255(a)(3) does reach zero percent - in the twentieth year after the section 126 payments were received - but the collection holds no receipt date and line 29a is the PRODUCT rather than the factors, so nothing in this graph can tell a genuinely zero line 29a from an unanswered one. The section 1252 twin can, because ../writableFarmlandFullYearsHeld asks for the band. Each refuses. COMPLETE-SAFETY: five complete-safe class wrappers and nothing else, so this gate cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item, and it is Complete-FALSE on every committed scenario. THE SUCCESSOR THE PARAGRAPHS ABOVE NAME HAS BEEN BUILT, and the section 1252 plus section 1255 pair - the one pair those paragraphs call real and expected - is no longer refused. Read the argument above as the history of this gate and this bracket as its present scope. WHAT CHANGED. ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution gained a SIXTH case, tested first, whose condition names BOTH classes, and it ADDS line 27c to line 29b instead of switching between them; ../section1255OrdinaryRecaptureContribution now performs the printed Line 29b reduction on every item, subtracting line 27c from the line 24 gain before the minimum against line 29a. Fact.Name: Line 27a multiplied by the IRC 1252(a)(3) applicable percentage (Form 4797 Part III line 27b)

Leg (A) is line 29a; leg (B) is line 24; this is the minimum. Line 29a arrives with the applicable percentage already applied, which is what the printed caption asks for. THE REDUCTION BELOW IS NOW PERFORMED, and the paragraph that follows is the history of this fact rather than its present body. Read them in that order. WHAT THE BODY DOES NOW: line 24 is floored at zero, line 27c is SUBTRACTED from it, and the minimum is taken against line 29a - the printed Line 29b rule exactly as quoted below, applied on every item rather than only on the pair. IT MOVES NO COMMITTED VALUE. The subtrahend is GATED ON THE CLASS ATTESTATION, so on an item that does not attest section 1252 farm land it is a literal $0 and subtracting it is the identity. The gate is not decoration: the instruction subtracts "the part of the gain treated as ordinary income under the other provision", and on an item that does not attest section 1252 no part of its gain is - ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution takes that item's own class block, never line 27c. Reading line 27c ungated would also have been Complete $0 on the whole committed corpus, on the weaker proof /section1252OrdinaryRecapture rests on (an unanswered line 27a reads $0 and the applicable percentage of $0 is $0), but that proof assumes which questions the filer was asked; this one does not. NO NEW FLOOR IS NEEDED ON THE SUBTRACTION and none is written, because none could ever fire: line 27c is itself the minimum of line 27b and line 24 floored at zero, so it can never exceed the figure it is subtracted from. A floor here would be unreachable code. THE "See instructions" ON LINE 29b WAS A REDUCTION THIS FACT DID NOT PERFORM, and the reason was that the population it applies to was refused rather than computed. The instruction reads: "If any part of the gain shown on line 24 is treated as ordinary income under sections 1231 through 1254 (for example, section 1252), enter the smaller of (a) line 24 reduced by the part of the gain treated as ordinary income under the other provision, or (b) line 29a." An item reaching this fact attested section 1255 and NO other modeled class, because ../hasContradictoryFarmlandOrCostSharingClassAttestation refused the multi-class item outright - so no part of its line 24 was ordinary income under another provision, the reduction clause was VACUOUS, and line 29b was the plain minimum. That guard carried the full argument and named the successor the reduction owed; that successor is the 2026-09-20 amendment above. THE GreaterOf FLOOR IS ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution's OWN, reused rather than re-derived: line 24 may be negative, and a negative minimum would make the recapture negative, which is not a thing line 29b can be. NOTE WHICH OPERAND IS CAPPED. The minimum caps the recapture at the GAIN, not line 29a at the payments. NO WORKSHEET TAIL: section 126 property is not section 1250 property, so ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent is $0 for this item. NON-NEGATIVE, integer cents. Consumed by ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution and by /section1255OrdinaryRecapture (a legibility head with no second addend).

Fact.Name: Ordinary recapture for this property (Form 4797 Part III line 25b, 26g, 27c, 28b or 29b, into line 31)
Fact.Description: [this fact is SIX-cased. The first case is the ORDERED section 1252 plus section 1255 pair and it is the one exception to "exactly ONE block per property" that the two brackets below assert: it ADDS line 27c and line 29b, because the printed Line 29b instruction orders those two blocks against each other for exactly this property and the printed line 31 adds them. Every other case still takes one block. An item attesting any OTHER pair is still refused upstream rather than assigned an arm here. Read the two paragraphs below as this fact's history.] SIX CASES: the first ADDS line 27c and line 29b for an item attesting BOTH section 1252 and section 1255; then one arm per class - section 1245 (line 25b), section 1250, section 1254, section 1252 (line 27c) and section 1255 (line 29b). The printed line 31 adds them all; any other multi-class attestation among sections 1252, 1254 and 1255 is refused upstream rather than assigned an arm here. The paragraph below describes the first three arms. THE PER-ITEM ADDEND OF THE PRINTED LINE 31, class-switched since 2026-08-04 and three-armed since 2026-08-17: line 25b on the section 1245 arm, line 26g on the section 1250 arm, line 28b on the section 1254 arm. Line 31 is "Add property columns A through D, lines 25b, 26g, 27c, 28b, and 29b. Enter here and on line 13" - ONE printed join across BOTH class blocks, which is why this fact keeps its path, its name and its consumers, and why /section1245OrdinaryRecapture already IS line 31 without a second return-level aggregate under it. THE SECTION 1245 ARM (line 25b) = the smaller of line 24 (total gain, floored at 0) and line 25a (depreciation allowed) = ALL the depreciation, up to the gain, independent of the holding period. THE SECTION 1250 ARM (line 26g) = ../section1250OrdinaryRecaptureContribution = only the EXCESS of actual depreciation over straight line, up to the gain. The rest of the depreciation is not ordinary income at all; it is unrecaptured section 1250 gain and leaves through ../unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent into the 25% rate group. THE SECTION 1245 ARM IS TESTED FIRST, which decides the one case the two attestations can both be true in. A property cannot be both classes; if a filer answers both, this Switch recaptures ALL the depreciation rather than only the excess, which is the conservative direction FOR A TRUTHFULLY ENTERED PAIR (line 25b is never smaller than line 26g for the same property, because the excess over straight line cannot exceed the total - an inequality the tree does not enforce, since line 26a is uncapped by design; see ../isSection1245Property for why every consequence of inverting it stays adverse or neutral). THE SECTION 1254 ARM (line 28b) = ../section1254OrdinaryRecaptureContribution = the expenditures the taxpayer DEDUCTED instead of capitalizing - the section 263/616/617 costs and the section 611 depletion - up to the gain. ITS CASE IS EXPLICIT, not a fall-through: a multi-class section 1254 item never reaches any arm, because ../hasContradictorySection1254ClassAttestation refuses it at ../isInScope - line 28b is ordered against neither line 25b nor line 26g by anything printed, and Switch position is not an ordering argument. It is neither of the other two: section 1245 gives back depreciation, section 1250 gives back the excess over straight line, and section 1254 gives back deductions that never entered basis at all. There is no unrecaptured-gain tail behind it, so a section 1254 item's whole non-recapture remainder is a section 1231 amount. CASE 2'S CONDITION BECAME EXPLICIT ON 2026-08-17 and the change is worth naming because it moves no committed value. It read ../isInScope alone, which was sound while ../isInScope's Any had exactly TWO members: reaching case 2 then meant the section 1245 attestation was false and the section 1250 one true. The Any has THREE members now, so that implication is gone and ../isSection1250PropertyComplete is written down. Every item that took case 2 before still takes it; the section 1254 arm is the new case 3, and reaching IT means both of the other class attestations are false. Defined ONLY for an in-scope disposition; for a refused disposition (an item attesting NO modeled printed class, an unanswered-holding-period loss - the holding-period re-derivation, a sub-threshold livestock LOSS whose month count or class question is unanswered - 2026-08-03, an attested section 1250 GAIN whose line 26a is unanswered - 2026-08-04, an attested section 1254 GAIN whose line 28a is unanswered - 2026-08-17, or a MULTI-CLASS item attesting section 1254 alongside section 1245 or section 1250 - 2026-08-17) this resolves Result.Incomplete (a Switch with no default arm), which propagates through /section1245OrdinaryRecapture and /form4797OrdinaryIncome to /totalIncome and refuses the return rather than compute an unsupported or misrouted disposition (World-#1-safe).

Fact.Name: Non-recapture remainder (section 1231 excess or loss)
Fact.Description: The part of the total gain/(loss) that is NOT ordinary section 1245 recapture = line 24 total gain minus line 25b recapture. A positive value is a section 1231 EXCESS (sold above original cost); a negative value is a section 1231 / Part II LOSS (recapture is 0, so the remainder equals the whole negative total gain); zero when the gain is fully recaptured. Inherits Result.Incomplete from the recapture for a REFUSED disposition (refusal propagates). That sentence named "a section 1250 disposition" as the refusal until 2026-08-04; a section 1250 item is now in scope and its remainder is line 24 minus line 26g, which is a LARGER remainder than a section 1245 item with the same depreciation would leave, because section 1250 recaptures only the excess over straight line. The refusals that still propagate here are an item attesting NEITHER printed class, an unanswered-holding-period loss, a sub-threshold livestock loss on an unanswered intake, and an attested section 1250 gain whose line 26a is unanswered.

Fact.Name: This disposition's gain as gross farm income (Pub. 505's Form 4797 livestock item)
Fact.Description:
The item's total gain when it IS draft/breeding/dairy/sporting livestock, else 0 — the per-item term of /farmLivestockGainsFromForm4797. Pub. 505's form-line map for gross income from farming names "Your gains from sales of draft, breeding, dairy, or sporting livestock shown on Form 4797" as one of its four items, and this is that item, computed per disposition.
IT REUSES THE CARVE-OUT THAT ALREADY EXISTS rather than adding an intake. ../isLivestockComplete is the the holding-period re-derivation/the holding-period re-derivation attestation this module has carried since 2026-07-31, and its definition is word-for-word Pub. 505's population — "livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy, or sporting purposes". So this leg needed no new question of the filer, which is why it is a derived fact and not a writable.
TWO FILL DECISIONS, BOTH UNPRINTED, BOTH STATED HERE rather than buried. (1) WHICH GAIN: ../totalGain, Form 4797 Part III line 24, the whole realized gain — not ../section1231Component. The printed words are "gains ... SHOWN ON Form 4797", and the gain shown for such a disposition is the total; splitting it into a recapture part and a section 1231 remainder is a CHARACTER question about how the gain is taxed, not about how much gross income the farm produced. A successor who disagrees should note that the two differ only when depreciation recapture is present. (2) FLOORED AT 0 PER ITEM: a disposition at a LOSS contributes 0, not a negative. The printed word is "gains", and this figure is a GROSS INCOME term — letting one animal's loss reduce another's gain would net inside a gross figure, which no printed instruction sanctions. The cost is disclosed: a farmer with a losing livestock sale gets a slightly LARGER numerator than a netting reading would give, which in the two-thirds test is taxpayer-FAVOURABLE, the opposite direction from ground (d)'s line-42 error.
A NON-LIVESTOCK DISPOSITION CONTRIBUTES 0 HERE even when it is plainly farm property — and that is the printed list's own boundary, not an oversight. See /farmLivestockGainsFromForm4797 for the Pub. 225 example that puts a MACHINERY gain in the farm column, which no printed list supports and which this dictionary does not follow. interpretation:provisional.

NOT A SCHEDULE E LINE 42 LEG, which is the confusion most likely to arise given the three K-1 aggregates that look like it. THE PUB. 225 DIVERGENCE THIS FACT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FOLLOW, recorded because it is the only published numeric example of the test and it disagrees with every printed list. Pub. 225 chapter 15's Example 1 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p225.pdf, page 91) puts BOTH a "Livestock Gain (Form 4797)" of 5,000 AND a "Machinery Gain (Form 4797)" of 25,000 in its farm column, and its farm total of 105,000 cannot be reached without the machinery. No printed list names machinery — not Pub. 505's four items, not Pub. 225's own three-item map, not Pub. 225's own narrative bullets, which say LIVESTOCK. This fact follows the LISTS. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a farmer with a machinery gain gets a smaller numerator here than the IRS's own example would give them, which understates the ratio and is TAXPAYER-ADVERSE. Resolving it needs a source this repo does not hold; the open question is carried on the two-thirds contract. interpretation:provisional.

Fact.Name: This property's unrecaptured section 1250 gain (Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet lines 1-3)
Fact.Description: The Schedule D Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's lines 1 through 3, which are PER PROPERTY and therefore live here rather than on Schedule D. Line 1: "If you have a section 1250 property in Part III of Form 4797 for which you made an entry in Part I of Form 4797 (but not on Form 6252), enter the smaller of line 22 or line 24 of Form 4797 for that property." Line 2: "Enter the amount from Form 4797, line 26g, for the property for which you made an entry on line 1." Line 3: "Subtract line 2 from line 1." WHAT IT IS, IN ONE SENTENCE: the depreciation this property gave back as gain but did NOT give back as section 1250 ORDINARY recapture - the slice taxed in the 25% rate group instead of at the long-term capital gain rate, which is why omitting it would be taxpayer-favourable and why it is built in the same unit as the recapture. FOUR GATES, each from a printed clause of line 1 or from the item's own admission. (1) "A SECTION 1250 PROPERTY" - ../isSection1250PropertyComplete. A section 1245 item has no line 26g and gives back all its depreciation as ordinary income already. (2) NOT A CONTRADICTORY BOTH-ATTESTED ITEM - Not(../isSection1245PropertyComplete). Such an item is recaptured under line 25b by ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution's positional Switch, so a line-3 slice computed against a line 26g nobody used would double-count it. The two facts agree on which arm the item is on because they test the same pair of wrappers. (2b) "IN PART III OF FORM 4797" - ../isInScope. A refused item is entered on no line of the form at all, because the return does not complete. COMPLETE-SAFE: ../isInScope reads only per-item complete-safe wrappers and the item's own arithmetic, exactly as its three guards do. (3) "FOR WHICH YOU MADE AN ENTRY IN PART I OF FORM 4797" - ../routesToSection1231. A property held one year or less never reaches Part I: the instructions say "for property held 1 year or less, do not complete Part III; instead, use Part II", and this module routes its whole non-recapture remainder to ../partIIOrdinaryComponent as ORDINARY income; so does an item IRC 1231(b)(1) excludes and de minimis safe-harbor property, whose remainder is ordinary whatever the holding period. THE ZERO-REMAINDER CASE NEEDS NO FOURTH GATE, provably. A fully recaptured item has line 24 = line 26g = min(line 24, line 26a), so line 26a is at least line 24; since the excess over straight line cannot exceed the total depreciation, line 22 is at least line 24 too, so line 1 = line 24 and line 3 = 0 on its own arithmetic. THE FLOOR IS NOT PRINTED AT LINE 3 and is justified from the per-property rule instead: "If you had more than one property described on line 1, complete lines 1 through 3 for each property on a separate worksheet. Enter the total of the line 3 amounts for all properties on line 3." Each property's line 3 is computed on its OWN sheet before the total is taken, so one property's negative may not net against another's positive. On a LOSS item line 1 is the negative line 24 and line 3 would be negative without it. (Line 1's other exclusion, "(but not on Form 6252)", needs no gate: an installment sale is not a /section1245Dispositions item at all, and its slice is worksheet line 4, scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252.) ROUNDING SITS HERE, ONE STEP EARLIER THAN THE WORKSHEET'S OWN DISCIPLINE, and the seam is named rather than left for a reader to trip on. This module rounds per item (the ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution convention, which the sizing contract specified for this fact too); the Schedule D worksheet block carries ONE Round, at scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250Gain, and every line between says "UNROUNDED" in as many words - including scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3, which sums this fact. So line 3 is an unrounded sum of rounded per-property terms. The divergence is bounded by 50 cents per property and arises only when ../depreciationAllowed carries cents AND binds the line-1 minimum; it is disclosed here rather than resolved, because moving the Round would put this fact out of step with every other per-item fact in the module. NON-NEGATIVE, integer cents. CONSUMED CROSS-MODULE by scheduleD:/unrecapturedSection1250GainLine3, which sums it across properties. COMPLETE-SAFETY: every gate is a complete-safe wrapper or per-item arithmetic, and the section 1250 branch is reached only on an item whose class question is answered, so this fact is Complete on every return - including one whose Form 4797 refuses for some other reason, which is what keeps the Schedule D block from turning one refusal into six - with ONE exception: an in-scope section 1250 item whose holding period is neither answered nor dated has no decided Part I entry, takes neither case, and is Incomplete (never a Placeholder zero) until the question is answered.

Fact.Name: Section 1231 gain from installment sales (Form 4797 Part I line 4, from Form 6252 line 26 or 37)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part I line 4, "Section 1231 gain from installment sales from Form 6252, line 26 or 37" — the filer's own Form 6252 figure, entered as a carry-IN attestation. The graph models Form 6252 (dictionary/ty2025/form6252.xml exports each sale's line 26 and line 37), and /form6252Sales/*/form4797Line4Amount carries them here; this entry is the line only on a return that files no Form 6252 (the same posture as /writableNonrecapturedSection1231Loss and as Schedule D's /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252, which attests a DIFFERENT slice of the same sale). NON-NEGATIVE, and the sign is read off the form rather than chosen: the printed line says section 1231 GAIN from installment sales, with no "(loss)" branch, where line 5 one line below it says "Section 1231 gain or (loss) from like-kind exchanges" — the internal contrast that settles it. The instructions say the same thing in words: "Enter any gain from the installment sale on Form 4797, line 4 or line 15, as applicable." A Min 0 Limit enforces it. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means no installment sale, so /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales is 0 and every existing return is byte-identical. WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not derivable from Schedule D's /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252 and does not bound it. Form 6252 line 26/37 carries the section 1231 gain; the unrecaptured section 1250 portion of it is a SUBSET the filer allocates through the three-step procedure at https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 12, and a Max limit tying the two would refuse correct returns where one property's section 1231 gain sits beside another property's section 1250 slice. READ ONLY when the return files no Form 6252: otherwise line 4 is read from the Form 6252 sales (/form6252Sales/*/form4797Line4Amount).

Fact.Name: Section 1231 gain from installment sales (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: /writableSection1231GainFromInstallmentSales when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means the return reports no installment sale, so Form 4797 Part I line 4 contributes nothing and /netSection1231GainOrLoss is what it was before this fact existed. Always resolves Complete, which is what lets it be added OUTSIDE the /claimsSection1245Disposition gate below without any risk of an Incomplete reaching a return that reports no disposition at all. WHY THIS LINE WAS BUILT FIRST. Form 4797 Part I lines 3 (Form 4684), 5 (Form 8824) and 6 (line 32) were absent from the sum when this fact landed; all three are now addends of /netSection1231GainOrLoss. Line 4 came first because it had a LIVE CONSUMER already asking about the same transaction: Schedule D's /writableUnrecapturedSection1250GainFromForm6252 attests the unrecaptured section 1250 slice of exactly this sale, and the worksheet caps that answer against Form 4797 line 7. When the return files a Form 6252 (/form4797HasFiledForm6252Sale), this line is read from the Form 6252 sales instead (/form6252Sales/*/form4797Line4Amount) and the typed carry-in is not read.

Fact.Name: Casualty or theft gain from Form 4684 line 39 (Form 4797 Part I line 3)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part I line 3, "Gain, if any, from Form 4684, line 39" — a verbatim pass-through of form4684:/sectionBNetGainToForm4797, which is where Form 4684 Section B Part II's line 36 / line 37 branch is computed and where the reason this figure is non-negative is argued. NON-NEGATIVE by that branch's own condition, which is also what the printed line assumes when it says "Gain, if any": the line-39 branch is taken exactly when the long-term loss total is at most the long-term gain total, so the combine cannot go below zero. No Min-0 Limit is written here, because a floor would MASK a Form 4684 error rather than prevent one. AN ADDEND OF LINE 7, NOT A REPLACEMENT FOR ANY OTHER. Part I line 7 is "Combine lines 2 through 6"; this module models line 2 as the per-disposition section 1231 components, line 4 as /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales, and now line 3 as this fact. Lines 5 (Form 8824) and 6 (line 32, from other than casualty or theft) still have no intake and still enter as nothing at all — an UNDER-statement, never the reverse. IT SITS OUTSIDE THE /claimsSection1245Disposition GATE, deliberately, and for the same reason line 4 does: a filer whose only Form 4797 Part I amount is a Form 4684 line-39 gain has no /section1245Dispositions item at all, so an addend inside the gate would leave the very population this change exists for at $0 — and the Schedule D Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's block header ("If you aren't reporting a gain on Form 4797, line 7, skip lines 1 through 9") reads that same line 7. ALWAYS COMPLETE ON A RETURN WITH NO CASUALTY CLAIM: form4684:/sectionBNetGainToForm4797 is gated through column totals that are themselves gated by form4684:/claimsCasualtyLoss, so it resolves Complete $0 there, never Result.Incomplete — which is what lets this be an addend outside every gate. On a return whose Section B holding period is REQUIRED and unanswered it is Result.Incomplete, and this fact and /netSection1231GainOrLoss go with it: the return stops rather than reporting a section 1231 gain sorted by a guess. LINE 18a IS THE OTHER HALF OF THIS ROUTE, gated on this same line 3: see /casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss, whose Description states how it is modeled.

Fact.Name: Net section 1231 gain or (loss) for the year (Form 4797 Part I)
Fact.Description:
The sum of the per-disposition section 1231 components (the non-recapture remainders of the dispositions held more than one year), Form 4797 Part I. May be a net gain (> 0) or a net loss (<= 0). Gated by /claimsSection1245Disposition (Complete-0 with no disposition). Drives the recharacterization: a net loss is ordinary (Part II); a net gain is ordinary up to the nonrecaptured section 1231 losses, the rest long-term capital gain.
EXPORTED for the Schedule D unrecaptured-section-1250 worksheet, which reads THIS line and not the recharacterized outputs below it. That worksheet's line 7 is "Enter the smaller of line 6 or the gain from Form 4797, line 7" and its block header is "If you aren't reporting a gain on Form 4797, line 7, skip lines 1 through 9 and go to line 10" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13) — both name Form 4797 line 7, which is this fact. The already-exported /section1231LtcgPortion is Form 4797 line NINE and is NOT a substitute; see its own Description for why.
WHAT THIS EXPORT CARRIES: the per-disposition section 1231 components AND Form 4797 Part I LINE 4, /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales ("Section 1231 gain from installment sales from Form 6252, line 26 or 37"). Line 4 is the installment sale the Schedule D worksheet's own line 4 attests the section 1250 slice of; before it was built, a filer whose ONLY trade-or-business disposition was such a sale reported no Form 4797 line 7 gain here, so the worksheet's block header ("If you aren't reporting a gain on Form 4797, line 7, skip lines 1 through 9") discarded their honest line-4 answer. THE LINE-4 ADDEND SITS OUTSIDE THE /claimsSection1245Disposition GATE, deliberately: that filer has no /section1245Dispositions item at all, so an addend inside the gate would leave the very population the build exists for at $0. The collection read stays strictly BEHIND the gate — the Switch's true arm adds line 4 to the CollectionSum, its default arm returns line 4 alone — so a return that never populates the collection still never reads it. WHAT LINE 7 ADDS TODAY ("Combine lines 2 through 6"). The Switch's true arm (a return with a /section1245Dispositions item) adds six terms: line 6, the CollectionSum of /section1245Dispositions/*/section1231Component; line 2, /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal (the typed Part I rows) and /form4797Line2Section1231FromScheduleK1 (Schedule K-1 box 10); line 3, /casualtyGainFromForm4684; line 4, /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales; and line 5, /section1231GainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges. The default arm adds the same terms without the collection read, so the collection stays strictly behind the /claimsSection1245Disposition gate while a filer whose only Part I amount is a line 2, 3, 4 or 5 figure still reaches line 7. Every term is complete-safe on a return that never answers its intake. Lines 3 and 4 are never negative. Lines 2 and 5 can be: the typed line 2 rows, and a Schedule K-1 box 10 LOSS that is answered as not from a passive activity (/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 admits it in full, as the partner instructions require), can lower line 7. A passive box 10 loss is not on line 2; it goes through Form 8582 first.

Fact.Name: Unanswered passivity question on a Schedule K-1 box 10 LOSS (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: True when this K-1's box 10 is answered, is NEGATIVE, and scheduleE:../writableK1065Box10IsFromPassiveActivity is UNANSWERED - the one state ../section1231GainForForm4797 has no arm for. It exists to make that refusal LEGIBLE rather than a silent Result.Incomplete arriving at /totalIncome from nowhere. COMPLETE-SAFETY: it reads only this K-1's own two raw leaves, never a flow-derived fact, so it cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without a box 10 loss. Complete-FALSE on every K-1 with no box 10, with a box 10 gain, or with the passivity question answered.

Fact.Name: Schedule K-1s carrying a box 10 LOSS whose passivity question is unanswered
Fact.Description: The sub-collection of scheduleE:/formK1s whose ../hasUnansweredPassivityOnBox10Loss is true. Used to compute the taxpayer-level refusal flag, the /section1245DispositionsUnsupported shape on a different collection.
