Fact.Description: True when any Schedule K-1 on the return reports a NEGATIVE box 10 net section 1231 amount and has not answered whether it comes from a passive activity. When true, /formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 resolves Result.Incomplete for that K-1, so /form4797Line2Section1231FromScheduleK1, /netSection1231GainOrLoss and /totalIncome resolve Result.Incomplete and the return refuses to complete - and this flag makes that refusal legible. Complete-false on every return with no such K-1, which is every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: This partnership or S corporation K-1's net section 1231 GAIN
Fact.Description: This Schedule K-1 (Form 1065 or Form 1120-S) item's contribution to Form 4797 Part I line 2, column (g). The Partner's Instructions for box 10 admit BOTH signs - "If the amount is either (a) a loss that isn't from a passive activity or (b) a gain, report it in column (g) of Form 4797, line 2" - and this fact carries both arms. FOUR ARMS AND NO DEFAULT. Box 10 unanswered is $0, so a /formK1s item recorded for its ordinary income alone contributes a Complete $0 and the CollectionSum over the collection stays Complete. A box 10 GAIN is admitted in full, whatever the activity, because the instructions admit it either way. A box 10 LOSS is admitted in full when the partner attests scheduleE:../writableK1065Box10IsFromPassiveActivity FALSE. A box 10 LOSS from a PASSIVE activity of a publicly traded partnership under the section 469(k) regime enters negated as scheduleE:../ptpSection1231PassiveLossAllowedOnForm4797, the part the partner instructions' PTP procedure allows against the same partnership's own income (all of it on the entire disposition of the interest), the rest carried forward on Schedule E. Any other box 10 LOSS from a PASSIVE activity is $0 here, and stays $0 deliberately: the instructions route it to "Passive Loss Limitations in the Instructions for Form 4797". THE POOL THAT ROUTE NAMES IS BUILT IN THIS DICTIONARY, not absent from it - scheduleE carries a full section 469 pipeline on this SAME /formK1s collection (scheduleE:/formK1s/*/lossIsPassive, .../nonpassiveAllowedLoss, .../passiveSuspendedLoss, .../line28ColumnGSuspendedShare, scheduleE:/section8582Magi), built from the K-1's activity loss. What is true is narrower: the box 10 section 1231 amount is not a member of that pool, because admitting it would require a new pool member this change does not build. So the $0 here is not a case of "no route exists" - it is "the route exists and this box 10 amount is not wired onto it," and the partner's box 10 loss is DROPPED for the year rather than suspended for a future one, even though section 469 does not disallow it outright and Form 8582 pooling could allow part or all of it against other passive income. Admitting it to line 2 unpooled would be the worse of the two wrong answers: a passive loss netting against section 1231 gains with no section 469 limitation applied at all. THE FIFTH STATE HAS NO ARM, WHICH IS THE REFUSAL. A negative box 10 whose passivity question is UNANSWERED falls off the end of the Switch and resolves Result.Incomplete, so the return refuses rather than silently dropping the loss. /hasUnansweredScheduleK1Box10Passivity makes that refusal legible. Both silent defaults are wrong in a named direction: dropping the loss costs a nonpassive partner the deduction AND the entry into the section 1231(c) recapture pool that would shelter a later year's gain, and admitting it lets a passive loss bypass section 469. The Schedule K-1 (Form 1120-S) twin is box 9, "Net section 1231 gain (loss)", and this module reads the same leaf for it because scheduleE records both entity types on the one /formK1s collection. A form4797 fact living on scheduleE's /formK1s collection, the cross-module shape scheduleD:/formK1s/*/collectiblesGainForScheduleD uses on the same collection.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 - the Schedule K-1 box 10 section 1231 gains
Fact.Description:
The total of every recorded Schedule K-1's box 10 section 1231 GAIN, the amount the partner instructions tell the filer to enter in column (g) of Form 4797 line 2 ("Don't complete columns (b) through (f) of Form 4797, line 2. Instead, enter 'From Schedule K-1 (Form 1065)' across these columns"). A CollectionSum of /formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797 behind an IsComplete guard on the scheduleE collection root, because a CollectionSum over a collection the return never opened does not resolve; a return with no K-1 reads a Complete $0 and /netSection1231GainOrLoss stays Complete everywhere it already was.
CAN BE NEGATIVE. Its per item terms admit a box 10 GAIN in full and also a NONPASSIVE box 10 LOSS in full (/formK1s/*/section1231GainForForm4797's third and fourth arms), so this CollectionSum can lower Form 4797 line 7 exactly as the printed instructions require for a nonpassive loss. The two per item states that never lower this sum are a PASSIVE box 10 loss (held at $0) and a negative box 10 whose passivity question is unanswered (which refuses the return instead of contributing any value); see the per item fact for both.

Fact.Name: Nonrecaptured section 1231 losses from the previous 5 years (carry-IN)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer's NET section 1231 losses DEDUCTED during the previous 5 years - included only to the extent they were taken into account in figuring taxable income - that have not yet been applied against a net section 1231 gain (Pub 544 "Nonrecaptured section 1231 losses"; the Form 4797 line 8 definition's four limbs: NET per-year losses, the 5 preceding tax years only, not yet applied against a net section 1231 gain, and actually deducted / taken into account), entered as a POSITIVE amount - the carry-IN posture: prior-year state enters as an INPUT, the engine never computes it from a prior year. OPTIONAL (three-state): unanswered means 0 (no prior nonrecaptured loss), so a net section 1231 gain is entirely long-term capital gain and every existing scenario stays additive. When present it recharacterizes that much of the current-year net section 1231 gain as ORDINARY income.

Fact.Name: Nonrecaptured section 1231 losses (complete-safe)
Fact.Description:
/writableNonrecapturedSection1231Loss when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern). Unanswered means no prior nonrecaptured section 1231 loss, so a net section 1231 gain is fully long-term capital gain.
EXPORTED: this fact IS Form 4797 line 8 ("Nonrecaptured net section 1231 losses from prior years", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1), which the Schedule D unrecaptured-section-1250 worksheet's line 8 reads verbatim — "Enter the amount, if any, from Form 4797, line 8" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sd.pdf, page 13). The RAW carry-IN amount, not the min(gain, loss) that Form 4797 line 12 takes: /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary below applies that min, and the printed line 8 does not. Always Complete (the IsComplete wrapper), and NOT gated on /claimsSection1245Disposition — a return with no disposition still answers 0 here, which is what the consumer's own skip rule needs.

Fact.Name: Section 1231 ordinary portion (net loss, or gain recaptured against prior losses)
Fact.Description:
The ORDINARY part of the net section 1231 result (Pub 544 "Section 1231 Gains and Losses"): if the net section 1231 result is a LOSS (<= 0) the whole (negative) net is ordinary loss (Part II); if it is a GAIN (> 0) the ordinary part is the smaller of the net gain and the nonrecaptured section 1231 losses from the previous 5 years. One of the FOUR ordinary addends of /form4797OrdinaryIncome (THREE until the Form 4797 line 14 casualty leg, /casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss, landed 2026-08-03). Cent-exact vs the Pub 544 example: net gain 2,000, nonrecaptured loss 700 -> 700 ordinary.
THE /claimsSection1245Disposition ARM WAS REMOVED 2026-08-03, when Form 4797 Part I line 4 (/section1231GainFromInstallmentSales) became a second addend of /netSection1231GainOrLoss. That arm returned $0 whenever the return reported no section 1245 disposition, which used to be the same population as "no Form 4797 Part I amount" and now is not: an installment-sale filer has a Part I line 7 gain and no disposition, and the arm would have zeroed their ordinary portion while the gain itself flowed on to Schedule D — dropping the section 1231(c) lookback recapture and UNDER-stating ordinary income. REMOVING IT MOVES NOTHING ELSE, provably rather than by measurement. On a return with no Part I amount at all /netSection1231GainOrLoss is Complete-$0 (its own gate plus the complete-safe line-4 alias), so the GreaterThan below is false and the default arm returns that $0 — the same value, and the same Complete, the deleted arm produced.

Fact.Name: Section 1231 long-term capital gain portion (Form 4797 line 7 to Schedule D line 11)
Fact.Description:
The LONG-TERM CAPITAL GAIN part of a net section 1231 GAIN: the net section 1231 gain minus the ordinary portion recaptured against nonrecaptured prior-year losses = max(0, net section 1231 gain - nonrecaptured section 1231 loss). Zero when the net section 1231 result is a loss or fully recaptured as ordinary. Complete-safe additive: it is added into Schedule D line 15 (/longTermGainOrLossAfterCarryover) exactly like the box-2a capital-gain-distributions term, and every existing return adds 0. Cent-exact vs the Pub 544 example: net gain 2,000, nonrecaptured loss 700 -> 1,300 long-term capital gain. EXPORTED for the Schedule D handoff. DISCLOSED ARTIFACT: when the return refuses because some OTHER disposition is knocked out (e.g. an unanswered-holding-period loss alongside an answered long-term gain), this fact can still resolve Complete and export into Schedule D while /form4797OrdinaryIncome and /totalIncome are Result.Incomplete - World-#1 holds because no return completes (tax is never computed from the partial state), but the intermediate LTCG value is visible in the snapshot.
THIS IS FORM 4797 LINE 9, NOT LINE 7, and the distinction is load-bearing for anything downstream that quotes "Form 4797, line 7". This fact is max(0, line 7 gain - line 8); the Schedule D Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain Worksheet's line 9 is max(0, min(ITS line 6, the line 7 gain) - line 8), and the two agree only when that worksheet's line 6 is at least the Form 4797 line 7 gain — i.e. only when its own line-7 minimum picks the Form 4797 side. Substituting this fact there is therefore a defect that PASSES every test whose worksheet line 6 is the larger of the two, which is most of them. That worksheet reads /netSection1231GainOrLoss (line 7) and /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss (line 8) directly and does its own minimum.
THE /claimsSection1245Disposition ARM WAS REMOVED 2026-08-03 for the same reason it was removed from /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary above: since Form 4797 Part I line 4 (/section1231GainFromInstallmentSales) joined /netSection1231GainOrLoss, "no section 1245 disposition" no longer means "no Part I gain", and the arm would have held an installment- sale filer's long-term capital gain at $0 while /netSection1231GainOrLoss reported it — the worst of both directions, since the Schedule D worksheet's line-7 cap would have RISEN on the same return whose Schedule D line 11 gain the arm suppressed.

Fact.Name: Part II ordinary gain/(loss) from short-term (one year or less) section 1245 dispositions
Fact.Description: The sum of the per-disposition Part II ordinary components (the non-recapture remainders of the dispositions held one year or less, Form 4797 Part II line 10). May be a net ordinary gain or loss. Gated by /claimsSection1245Disposition (Complete-0 with no disposition). One of the FOUR ordinary addends of /form4797OrdinaryIncome (THREE until the Form 4797 line 14 casualty leg, /casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss, landed 2026-08-03).

Fact.Name: Net gain or (loss) from Form 4684 Section B business casualty or theft (Form 4797 line 14)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part II line 14 = "Net gain or (loss) from Form 4684, lines 31 and 38a" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1) - a verbatim pass-through of form4684:/sectionBNetGainOrLoss, which is where those two Form 4684 lines are computed (line 31 and line 38a are separate facts there, under the holding-period fork). SIGNED, and not always negative: form4684:/sectionBNetGainOrLoss is Form 4684 line 31 plus line 38a with a live column (c), so it can be POSITIVE - a short-term Section B casualty gain is ORDINARY income here, not a deduction addend; a Section B LOSS remains negative, matching the printed line's own "(loss)" parenthetical. FOURTH ADDEND OF LINE 17. This module does not model Part II line by line; it models line 17 ("Combine lines 10 through 16", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1) as /form4797OrdinaryIncome's sum of named addends, and this fact is the line-14 one. The map is: line 10 = /partIISection1245Ordinary, lines 11-12 = /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary, line 13 = /section1245OrdinaryRecapture, line 14 = HERE. Lines 15 and 16 (ordinary gain from Form 6252 installment sales and from Form 8824 like-kind exchanges) still have no intake and enter as nothing - an UNDER-statement of ordinary income, never the reverse. LINE 18a IS MODELED: /lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven, gated on a positive Form 4797 line 3 (the Form 4684 line-39 branch), whose two operands are this module's line 11 loss (/partIILossFromLineSeven) and form4684:/sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii, and whose destination is scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions. Line 18a reads "If the loss on line 11 includes a loss from Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii), enter that part of the loss here. Enter the loss from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1). The Form 4684 line-39 branch is disjoint from the line-38 branch that feeds form4684:/incomeProducingCasualtyLoss, so a live line 18a cannot double-count with the Schedule A line - https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040sca.pdf, page 11 prove "from Form 4684, lines 32 and 38b, OR Form 4797, line 18a" is ONE Schedule A line fed by exactly one of the two routes. 18a is $0 on every return with no Section B casualty gain (the entire committed corpus). LINE 18b IS NO LONGER EQUAL TO LINE 17: /form4797OrdinaryIncome adds line 18a back, which is what line 18b's "Redetermine the gain or (loss) on line 17 excluding the loss, if any, on line 18a. Enter here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), Part I, line 4" (lines 66-67) means. ADDITIVITY: form4684:/sectionBNetGainOrLoss is gated by form4684:/claimsCasualtyLoss and built from a per-event fact that is 0 on every event not attested Section B, so it resolves Complete 0 - never Result.Incomplete - on every return that predates the Section B arm, including the u066/u066b casualty scenarios that answer /claimsCasualtyLoss true. Adding it as an addend of /form4797OrdinaryIncome is therefore byte-identical for the whole existing corpus.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 11, the loss (if any) from line 7 — POSITIVE magnitude
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part II line 11, "Loss, if any, from line 7" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1), whose entry rule is printed on line 7 itself: "Individuals, partners, S corporation shareholders, and all others. If line 7 is zero or a loss, enter the amount from line 7 on line 11 below and skip lines 8 and 9" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1). Line 7 is /netSection1231GainOrLoss, so this is that fact negated when it is negative, and 0 otherwise. POSITIVE MAGNITUDE, and the reading is the consumer's own instruction rather than a convention chosen here: line 18a says "To figure which loss is smaller, treat both losses as positive numbers" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 9, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction), and the printed line 11 carries the parenthesis pair that marks a loss entry. Its one consumer, /lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven, compares it with form4684:/sectionBLongTermLossColumnBii, which is a positive magnitude for the same reason. THIS FACT IS NOT AN ADDEND OF ANYTHING. Line 11 already reaches line 17 inside /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary, whose Description has named "Part II lines 11-12" since it was written: on a net section 1231 LOSS that fact returns the whole (negative) net, which IS line 11. This fact exists so line 18a can read the same loss as a magnitude without re-deriving it; adding it anywhere else would double-count. COMPLETENESS: it inherits /netSection1231GainOrLoss's, which is Result.Incomplete on a return whose disposition is refused. That is why its consumer reads it BEHIND a line-3 gate rather than in a bare When - see that fact.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 18a — the Form 4684 line 35 column (b)(ii) part of the line 11 loss, to Schedule A line 16
Fact.Description: Form 4797 line 18a: "If the loss on line 11 includes a loss from Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii), enter that part of the loss here. Enter the loss from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16. (Do not include any loss on property used as an employee.) Identify as from 'Form 4797, line 18a.'" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1). Its instruction needs no interpretation: "You must complete this line if there is a gain on Form 4797, line 3; a loss on Form 4797, line 11; and a loss on Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii). Enter on this line the smaller of the loss on Form 4797, line 11, or the loss on Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii). To figure which loss is smaller, treat both losses as positive numbers. Enter the loss from income-producing property on Schedule A (Form 1040), line 16. Identify it as from 'Form 4797, line 18a.' Do not include any loss from property used as an employee." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 9, LEFT column of a TWO-COLUMN extraction). POSITIVE, like the two losses it chooses between and like its destination's siblings. THE THREE PRINTED CONDITIONS, and where each one is enforced. (1) "a gain on Form 4797, line 3" is the FIRST arm of the Switch below, tested and negated, so that every return without a Form 4684 line-39 gain returns a literal Dollar 0 without reading anything else. (2) "a loss on Form 4797, line 11" and (3) "a loss on Form 4684, line 35, column (b)(ii)" need no arm of their own: both operands are POSITIVE MAGNITUDES that are 0 exactly when the loss is absent, so the LesserOf is 0 whenever either condition fails. That is an equality, not an approximation - LesserOf(0, x) = 0 and LesserOf(x, 0) = 0 for non-negative x. WHY CONDITION (1) IS TESTED FIRST AND NOT FOLDED IN, two independent reasons, both load-bearing. THE FIRST IS ARITHMETIC: without it this fact would fire on a return whose Form 4684 Section B long-term losses EXCEED its gains, which is the Form 4684 LINE-38 branch, where form4684:/sectionBLongTermIncomeProducingLoss (line 38b) already carries the same column (b)(ii) loss to Schedule A line 16 - the two routes would DOUBLE-DEDUCT the one loss. The i1040sca line-16 closed list joins them with "or" for exactly this reason ("from Form 4684, lines 32 and 38b, or Form 4797, line 18a"), and the branch makes that "or" exclusive: line 39, hence any Form 4797 line-3 gain, fires only when line 37 is less than or equal to line 36, and lines 38a/38b fire only when it is more. THE SECOND IS COMPLETENESS: /partIILossFromLineSeven inherits /netSection1231GainOrLoss's Result.Incomplete on every return whose section 1245 disposition is refused, and this fact is an addend of scheduleA:/otherItemizedDeductions, which no form4797 fact reached before. Reading line 11 in a bare When would carry that Incomplete onto Schedule A line 16 for the whole refused-disposition population. The line-3 gate is complete-safe on its own (/casualtyGainFromForm4684 passes through a form4684 fact gated on form4684:/claimsCasualtyLoss), so the Switch short-circuits before line 11 is ever read. LINE 18b IS /form4797OrdinaryIncome, WHICH GAINS THIS FACT AS A FIFTH ADDEND. Line 18b is "Redetermine the gain or (loss) on line 17 excluding the loss, if any, on line 18a. Enter here and on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), Part I, line 4" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 1). Line 17 contains the WHOLE line-11 loss, so excluding the 18a part means ADDING this positive amount back. Before this change 18a was identically 0 and line 18b equalled line 17, which is why /form4797OrdinaryIncome could export line 17 unchanged. NOT MODELLED, AND NAMED RATHER THAN SILENT: "Do not include any loss from property used as an employee." This dictionary collects no employee-property attestation on a casualty event, so a column (b)(ii) loss on property used as an employee would be routed here. The population is not reachable today - every return with a Form 4797 line-3 gain is refused collection-wide by form4684:/knockoutCasualtyGain - and the same unmodelled exclusion already sits on form4684:/sectionBLongTermIncomeProducingLoss, whose printed line 38b carries the identical sentence, so this change neither created nor widened it.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 ordinary gain or (loss) (Form 4797 line 18 to Schedule 1 line 4)
Fact.Description: The taxpayer-level Form 4797 ORDINARY income (Form 4797 line 18b, "Redetermine the gain or (loss) on line 17 excluding the loss, if any, on line 18a") that flows to Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 4 ("Other gains or (losses)") and into /totalIncome. Derived from the printed line 17 (/partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen, which carries lines 10 through 16) plus the line 18a add-back (/lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven, modelled as a POSITIVE magnitude), so the Form 6252 and Form 8824 ordinary carry-ins on lines 15 and 16 reach Schedule 1 line 4. Line 17 sums FOUR of the FIVE addends this fact carries: /section1245OrdinaryRecapture (Part III LINE 31 depreciation recapture across both modeled classes - lines 25b and 26g - carried to Part II line 13) + /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary (net section 1231 loss, or net section 1231 gain recaptured against prior nonrecaptured losses; Part II lines 11-12) + /partIISection1245Ordinary (short-term Part II gain/loss, line 10) + /casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss (line 14, the Form 4684 Section B business casualty or theft net gain or loss); the FIFTH, line 18a's /lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven, is added back rather than summed into line 17 itself. May be a net loss (negative). The Name above says "line 18" rather than "line 18b" because line 18a is identically 0 on every return with no Form 4684 line-39 gain, so line 17 and line 18b are then the same number; it is left as written. Complete-0 for every return with no section 1245 disposition, no Section B casualty and no Form 4684 line-39 gain (byte-identical additive /totalIncome; the line-14 addend is gated by form4684:/claimsCasualtyLoss and resolves 0 for every event not attested Section B, and the line-18a addend's first Switch arm returns a literal Dollar 0 on every return without a Form 4684 line-39 gain, so neither carries an Incomplete into this sum - byte-identical additive for the whole existing corpus, which carries no Section B casualty gain at all). If ANY disposition is knocked out - the neither-printed-class complement (land, section 1252/1254/1255 classes, or an unanswered class PAIR), an UNANSWERED-holding-period LOSS, a SUB-THRESHOLD LIVESTOCK LOSS whose month count or class question is unanswered, or an attested SECTION 1250 GAIN whose line 26a is unanswered - /section1245OrdinaryRecapture is Result.Incomplete, so this and /totalIncome are Result.Incomplete and the return refuses (World-#1-safe). The LONG-TERM capital gain part is NOT here - it flows separately to Schedule D via /section1231LtcgPortion. EXPORTED for Schedule 1 and MeF.

Fact.Name: Gain from line 32, from other than casualty or theft (Form 4797 Part I line 6)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part I line 6, "Gain, if any, from line 32, from other than casualty or theft" the Part III remainder that returns to Part I. It NAMES an amount the graph already computes rather than adding a new one: /netSection1231GainOrLoss (Part I line 7, "Combine lines 2 through 6") adds this line (the CollectionSum of /section1245Dispositions/*/section1231Component) to line 2 (/form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal and /form4797Line2Section1231FromScheduleK1), line 3 (/casualtyGainFromForm4684), line 4 (/section1231GainFromInstallmentSales) and line 5 (/section1231GainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges): six terms when the return has a Part III item, the same five without this one otherwise. This fact is that same CollectionSum, so line 6 and line 7 foot by construction and NO obligation is owed. GATED on IsComplete(/section1245Dispositions) by the template, so a return that reports no disposition prints 0 rather than resolving Incomplete, which is the shape /farmLivestockGainsFromForm4797 already uses over the same collection. NOT ROUNDED a second time (params.round false): each ../section1231Component is the ../nonRecaptureRemainder, which is itself Round()ed, so the sum is already whole dollar and an extra Round would only risk diverging from the identical term line 7 consumes. THE ONE DIVERGENCE FROM THE PRINTED FORM, stated rather than hidden: the printed line 6 is a GAIN, because on paper a loss disposition never reaches Part III at all and is written on a Part I line 2 row instead. The Part I line 2 collection exists - /form4797Section1231Sales, summed onto line 7 by /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal - and it carries a typed loss row on line 2 exactly as the printed form does. What still lets THIS box print a negative is that every disposition attesting a printed line 19(a) class routes through /section1245Dispositions, so a class-attested item that cleared its holding period at a LOSS returns its remainder through line 32 to this line rather than to a line 2 row. Flooring it at 0 would be worse, not better: line 7 consumes the unfloored sum, so a floor would break the footing between the two printed lines while leaving the loss invisible. The remedy is a print one, not a computation: render such an item's remainder as a Part I line 2 row and floor this cell on the printed page, which is a change to the printed-form register, not to this fact; no dollar moves. CASUALTY IS ALREADY EXCLUDED, as the printed line requires: casualty and theft dispositions live in form4684:/casualtyEvents and reach Part III through /casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder, which returns on Form 4684 line 33 and never enters this collection. DISPOSITION refused: the carry-map audit asked line 6 to read /partIIILine32NonRecaptureRemainder instead of summing this collection leaf, and the printed form refuses the swap on three separate grounds. FIRST, line 32 is undivided and line 6 is one of its two portions: the printed line 32 reads "Enter the portion from casualty or theft on Form 4684, line 33. Enter the portion from other than casualty or theft on Form 4797, line 6", and /partIIILine32NonRecaptureRemainder is built on /partIIILine30TotalGainsAllProperties, which adds form4684:/casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture and form4684:/sectionBCasualtyGainsFromForm4797Line32 to the sale columns - so reading it here would carry the casualty portion onto Part I line 6, which is exactly what the printed line forbids. SECOND, line 32 also carries the SHORT holding period items: a /section1245Dispositions item that did not clear its class holding period, or that is property IRC 1231(b)(1) excludes or de minimis safe-harbor property, contributes its whole remainder to line 30 minus line 31 but contributes $0 here, because ../section1231Component gates on ../routesToSection1231 and routes those items to Part II line 10 through ../partIIOrdinaryComponent instead. On paper such an item never reaches Part III at all; in this graph it does, and line 6 is the fact that keeps it out of Part I. THIRD, the completeness semantics differ on purpose: /partIIILine32NonRecaptureRemainder resolves Result.Incomplete on a refused disposition, because line 31 does, while line 6 is complete-safe by its IsComplete gate so that a return with no disposition prints 0. NOTHING IS RETIRED: the audit called /partIIILine32NonRecaptureRemainder a duplicate derivation with no dependents, but it is the printed line-32 box (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS4797/en/configuration.yml f2_99[0]) and carries its own Export, so it is consumed by the register rather than orphaned.

Fact.Name: Total gain across the /section1245Dispositions property columns (Form 4797 Part III line 30, sale columns)
Fact.Description: The SALE share of Form 4797 Part III line 30, "Total gains for all properties. Add property columns A through D, line 24": Round(CollectionSum(/section1245Dispositions/*/totalGain)), $0 when the collection is unanswered. A HELPER of /partIIILine30TotalGainsAllProperties, which adds the casualty property columns that Form 4684 contributes to the same printed table. THE GUARD IS IsComplete(/section1245Dispositions) rather than /claimsSection1245Disposition, which is the gate /section1245OrdinaryRecapture (line 31) uses. The two differ only on a return whose disposition collection is complete and nonempty while /hasSection1245Disposition is unanswered or false, a state the flow does not produce; the guarded collection sum template offers the collection guard, and it is $0 on the same empty returns. SUMS EVERY REPORTED ITEM, in scope or not: line 30 is a printed total of the line 24 cells, and line 24 is defined for a refused item too. Line 31 is the fact that goes Result.Incomplete on a refused disposition, so the refusal still reaches the return through /partIIILine32NonRecaptureRemainder and /form4797OrdinaryIncome.

Fact.Name: Total gains for all properties (Form 4797 Part III line 30)
Fact.Description: THE PRINTED LINE 30: "Total gains for all properties. Add property columns A through D, line 24." Three addends, because the printed Part III table has two kinds of property column. /partIIILine30DispositionColumnsTotalGain is the line 24 total of the /section1245Dispositions sale columns. form4684:/casualtyPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture and form4684:/sectionBCasualtyGainsFromForm4797Line32 are together the line 24 total of the CASUALTY columns that i4684 Line 33 routes into this Part III: the first is the casualty share of line 31 and the second is the casualty share of line 32. PER EVENT THOSE TWO SUM BACK TO THE EVENT'S GAIN EXACTLY ONLY WHERE THE IRC 1245(b)(4)(B) TERM IS ZERO. form4684:/casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIIOrdinaryRecapture is capped at the RECOGNIZED gain PLUS the fair market value of non-section-1245 replacement property, and 1245(a)(1) recognizes the result "notwithstanding any other provision of this subtitle", so on a section 1033 election with a non-1245 replacement the recapture exceeds the recognized gain and the remainder (line 32's casualty share) is floored at 0 rather than going negative; line 30 then carries the CAPPED RECAPTURE rather than the gain. Line 32 still foots (13,000 - 13,000 = 0) because this fact is built on the floored remainder. The printed line 24 that would make line 25b's "smaller of line 24 or 25a" true on its own terms is NOT modelled for a casualty column; naming that is item (19)'s residual and is not built here. 13,000 IS PINNED AS A DECISION: line 30 = the recognized gain 6,000 would make line 32 = 6,000 - 13,000 = -7,000 on a printed box, the exact negative the floor exists to stop; line 30 = the realized gain 18,000 would make line 32 = 5,000, and line 32's own printed text sends that portion to Form 4684 line 33, so it would leave as section 1231 gain through lines 36/39 and the return would recognize the whole 18,000 - defeating the section 1033 election the return makes. 13,000 is the only value under which 30 - 31 = 32 foots AND section 1033 still defers. So this fact foots the printed table by construction and /partIIILine32NonRecaptureRemainder, which subtracts line 31 from it, is exactly the sum of the per item non recapture remainders plus the casualty remainder. Complete $0 on a return with neither a disposition nor a casualty.

Fact.Name: Subtract line 31 from line 30 (Form 4797 Part III line 32)
Fact.Description: THE PRINTED LINE 32: "Subtract line 31 from line 30. Enter the portion from casualty or theft on Form 4684, line 33. Enter the portion from other than casualty or theft on Form 4797, line 6." /partIIILine30TotalGainsAllProperties less /section1245OrdinaryRecapture, which is this module's name for line 31. THE RETURN LEVEL SCALAR THE BOX PRINTS, which is why this fact is needed even though the graph already routes both of the portions the line names: the casualty portion leaves through form4684:/casualtyEvents/*/sectionBPartIIILine32Remainder and totals in form4684:/sectionBCasualtyGainsFromForm4797Line32 (Form 4684 line 33), and the non casualty portion leaves through /section1245Dispositions/*/nonRecaptureRemainder into /netSection1231GainOrLoss (Form 4797 line 6). Neither is the printed line 32 box, which carries the undivided total. THE SPLIT IS ALREADY WIRED AND THIS FACT DOES NOT REWIRE IT: it adds no addend anywhere and changes no committed value. Result.Incomplete when a reported disposition is refused, because line 31 is, which is the module's existing refusal semantics.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 12, gain from line 7 or the amount from line 8
Fact.Description: THE PRINTED LINE 12: "Gain, if any, from line 7 or amount from line 8, if applicable". Line 9 spells the entry rule out in full: "If line 9 is zero, enter the gain from line 7 on line 12 below. If line 9 is more than zero, enter the amount from line 8 on line 12 below" - which is the SMALLER of the line 7 net section 1231 gain and the line 8 nonrecaptured section 1231 loss, and nothing at all when line 7 is zero or a loss (that loss prints on line 11, and lines 8 and 9 are skipped). /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary already computes that minimum on a net GAIN and returns the whole negative net on a net LOSS, so line 12 is exactly that fact floored at zero. PRINT ONLY, AND NOT A NEW ADDEND OF ANYTHING: line 12 already reaches line 17 inside /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary, whose description has named "Part II lines 11-12" since it was written, and adding this fact anywhere else would double count. It inherits that fact's completeness, which is Result.Incomplete on a return whose disposition is refused.

Fact.Description: The literal $0 that Form 4797 line 12 falls to when Part I line 7 is zero or a loss. Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 17, lines 10 through 16 combined
Fact.Description: THE PRINTED LINE 17: "Combine lines 10 through 16". SEVEN ADDENDS, one per modeled printed line, and TWO of them are line 10. /partIISection1245Ordinary is line 10 (the Part II ordinary components of the dispositions held one year or less). /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary is lines 11 and 12 together, as its own description has said since it was written: on a net section 1231 LOSS it is the whole negative net, which is line 11, and on a net GAIN it is the min(line 7, line 8) that line 12 prints. /section1245OrdinaryRecapture is line 13 (Part III line 31 recapture across the modeled classes). /casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss is line 14 (the Form 4684 Section B net). /partIIOrdinaryGainFromInstallmentSales is line 15 and /partIIOrdinaryGainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges is line 16, the two Form 6252 and Form 8824 carry ins landing with this fact. THIS IS LINE 17 AND NOT LINE 18b. /form4797OrdinaryIncome is line 18b: its appended paragraph says "THIS FACT IS NOW LINE 18b RATHER THAN LINE 17" because it carries a FIFTH addend, the line 18a loss /lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven added back, which line 17 does not. The two facts therefore differ by the line 18a add back, which is correct and printed, AND by the two new carry ins, which is the tracked debt those two intake facts declare: line 18b does not read them yet, so a return with a Form 6252 or Form 8824 ordinary amount prints a line 17 that its own line 18b does not foot to until /form4797OrdinaryIncome is rewired onto this fact. No other fact consumes this one, so it moves no dollar on any existing return. THE SEVENTH ADDEND IS THE OTHER HALF OF LINE 10. /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal is the complete-safe CollectionSum of /form4797OrdinaryDispositions/*/gainOrLoss, the typed Part II line 10 rows. It is NOT a double count of /partIISection1245Ordinary: the two collections are disjoint by their own definitions - a /form4797OrdinaryDispositions row is a disposition carrying none of the printed section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 classes, which is precisely what a /section1245Dispositions item must attest exactly one of - so the printed line 10 table is one table fed by two disjoint sources and line 17 must add both. The term is $0 on every return that never creates the collection, so no committed scenario moves.

Fact.Name: Section 179 recapture carried to income (Form 4797 line 35, column (a), floored at zero)
Fact.Description: The part of line 35 column (a) the return carries to income: /partIVLine35Section179RecaptureAmount when it is above zero, $0 when it is zero or negative, and $0 when line 33 column (a) is unanswered (no section 179 deduction to recapture).
