The printed line 35 keeps the plain subtraction the form prints. Read by /partIVLine35RecaptureToRoute.

Fact.Name: Section 280F(b)(2) recapture carried to income (Form 4797 line 35, column (b), floored at zero)
Fact.Description: The part of line 35 column (b) the return carries to income: /partIVLine35Section280FRecaptureAmount when it is above zero, $0 when it is zero or negative ("excess depreciation" is "the excess (if any)", IRC 280F(b)(2)(B)), and $0 when line 33 column (b) is unanswered. Incomplete when line 33 column (b) is answered and line 34 column (b) is not. Read by /partIVLine35RecaptureToRoute.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture the return must carry to income (both columns)
Fact.Description: /partIVLine35Section179RoutedAmount plus /partIVLine35Section280FRoutedAmount: the recapture the instructions send "as other income on the same form or schedule on which you took the deduction". $0 on every return that answers no Part IV line; Incomplete while a column is half answered. The amount the filer's allocation across schedules must equal (/partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated), and the "asked when" of the three allocation questions (above zero).

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture the filer allocated to a schedule (all destinations)
Fact.Description: The sum of the destinations now modeled: scheduleC:/scheduleCForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocatedTotal (Schedule C line 6, per business), scheduleF:/scheduleFForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocated (Schedule F line 8), income:/schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocated (Schedule 1 line 8z), scheduleE:/scheduleEForm4797Line35RecaptureAllocatedTotal (Schedule E line 3, per rental property), and form4835:/form4797Line35RecaptureAllocated (Form 4835 line 6). Each amount is complete safe, and a destination allocation counts only when the corresponding schedule is claimed, so an amount allocated to a schedule the return does not file counts $0 here rather than vanishing. Each carried destination leg reads this fact's gate (see /hasUnallocatedPartIVLine35Recapture).

Fact.Name: Form 4797 line 35 recapture is fully allocated to the schedules that carry it
Fact.Description: TRUE when /partIVLine35RecaptureAllocatedTotal equals /partIVLine35RecaptureToRoute, neither more nor less. The gate every destination leg reads (scheduleC:/scheduleCs/*/form4797Line35RecaptureLeg, scheduleF:/scheduleFForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg, income:/schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg, scheduleE:/rentalProperties/*/form4797Line35RecaptureLeg, form4835:/form4797Line35RecaptureLeg): TRUE lets each modeled leg carry its allocation, FALSE leaves each claimed destination Incomplete, so /totalIncome is Incomplete and the return refuses rather than dropping the recapture or counting it twice. Complete TRUE on every return with no Part IV amount and no allocation ($0 against $0), which is why no committed return moves. Incomplete while a column is half answered. A Schedule E royalty has no line-3 allocation in this model; its recapture remains unallocated and refuses instead of being moved to line 4 or Schedule 1 line 8z.

Fact.Name: Return has Form 4797 line 35 recapture not allocated to a schedule (refusal flag)
Fact.Description:
TRUE when /partIVLine35RecaptureIsAllocated is decided and FALSE: the line 35 recapture to carry differs from what the filer allocated to Schedule C line 6, Schedule F line 8, Schedule 1 line 8z, Schedule E rental-property line 3, and Form 4835 line 6. Every claimed modeled destination leg is then Incomplete, so /totalIncome is Incomplete and the return does not complete; this flag makes the refusal legible. THE REMEDY the application shows: allocate the whole line 35 amount to the schedule or schedules on which the deduction was taken. Schedule E royalty recapture has no modeled destination and still refuses under this flag. Complete false on every return with no Part IV amount, and false while a column is half answered (that return is Incomplete through the column itself).
[Correction to the sentence above: "Every claimed modeled destination leg is then Incomplete" is now true of the three legs that predate this campaign — Schedule C line 6, Schedule F line 8 and Schedule 1 line 8z — and NOT of the two added with the Schedule E and Form 4835 destinations, which contribute $0 on an unconfirmed allocation so that a pre-existing rental or farm-rental return keeps the line-3 and line-6 values it had before those legs existed (lead ruling of 2026-09-12: a new intake may not collapse a pre-existing return). The refusal itself is unchanged in reach: income:/schedule1Line8zForm4797Line35RecaptureLeg has no fallback, so /totalIncome stays Incomplete on every return this flag is true for, and this flag still makes that refusal legible.]

Fact.Name: Section 1231 gain or (loss) from like-kind exchanges (complete safe)
Fact.Description: /writableSection1231GainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges when answered, else 0 (the IsComplete pattern this module uses at /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales and /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss). Unanswered means the return reports no like kind exchange, so Form 4797 Part I line 5 contributes nothing. Always resolves Complete, which is what lets it be added OUTSIDE the /claimsSection1245Disposition gate: a filer whose only Part I amount is a Form 8824 section 1231 figure has no /section1245Dispositions item at all, so an addend inside that gate would leave exactly that population at 0, the argument /casualtyGainFromForm4684 and /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales each make in their own Descriptions. WIRED: /netSection1231GainOrLoss adds this fact as its Part I line 5 term in BOTH arms of its Switch. Because the wrapper is $0 on every return that never answers /writableSection1231GainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges, no committed scenario moves. When the return files a Form 8824 (/form4797HasFiledForm8824Exchange), this line is read from the Form 8824 exchanges instead (/form8824Exchanges/*/form4797Line5Amount) and the typed carry-in is not read.

Fact.Name: Section 1245 ordinary recapture for this property (Form 4797 Part III line 25b)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 25b, "Enter the smaller of line 24 or 25a": the printed section 1245 column cell for this property. It is ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution behind a section 1245 class gate, and that is exact rather than convenient: the first case of that Switch IS line 25b, Round(LesserOf(GreaterOf(line 24, 0), line 22 depreciation allowed)), and it is the case an item attesting section 1245 property takes. On an item that does not attest section 1245 property this resolves Complete $0, because the printed line 25 block is headed "If section 1245 property:" and a section 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 column leaves that cell empty. THE GATE IS WHAT MAKES THIS A SEPARATE FACT: ../section1250OrdinaryRecaptureContribution (line 26g), ../section1252OrdinaryRecaptureContribution (line 27c), ../section1254OrdinaryRecaptureContribution (line 28b) and ../section1255OrdinaryRecaptureContribution (line 29b) are each already zero on an item of another class, because their own inputs are complete safe zeros; line 25b's input is ../depreciationAllowed, which is nonzero on almost every column, so the raw computation would print a section 1245 recapture in the cell of a section 1250 property. THE NAME IS LINE SPECIFIC ON PURPOSE: the four facts named ...OrdinaryRecaptureContribution are ungated class computations, and this one is a gated printed cell, so it does not take that family name. A refused disposition makes ../ordinaryRecaptureContribution Result.Incomplete and this cell prints nothing, which is the module's existing refusal semantics.

Fact.Name: Subtract line 26a from line 24 (Form 4797 Part III line 26c, printed cell)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 26c, "Subtract line 26a from line 24": the printed section 1250 column cell for this property. ../section1250Line26cGainOverAdditionalDepreciation when the item attests section 1250 property, else Complete $0, because the printed line 26 block is headed "If section 1250 property" and a column of any other class leaves the cell empty. NOT FLOORED: a negative value is the form's own answer and is printed as such, and it is exactly the "line 24 isn't more than line 26a" arm of the printed skip rule that line 26e reads off the sign. CONSUMED, AND TAX-AFFECTING THROUGH LINE 26e: ../section1250Line26eSmallerOfLine26cOr26d takes the smaller of this cell and line 26d, ../section1250Line26e applies the skip rule to it, and ../section1250OrdinaryRecaptureContribution (line 26g) adds that cell, so a positive line 26c on pre-1976 property reaches line 31, Form 4797 line 13 and Schedule 1 line 4.

Fact.Name: Line 24 total gain less line 26a additional depreciation after 1975 (Form 4797 Part III line 26c, ungated)
Fact.Description: The arithmetic of Form 4797 Part III line 26c, "Subtract line 26a from line 24", before the section 1250 class gate: ../totalGain less ../additionalDepreciationAfter1975. A HELPER, not the printed cell: ../section1250Line26c is the printed cell and applies the class gate this fact deliberately does not, because the printed line 26 block is headed "If section 1250 property" and ../additionalDepreciationAfter1975 is a complete safe $0 on every other class, which would make this raw figure equal the whole gain on a section 1245 column. NOT FLOORED AT ZERO: the printed instruction is a plain subtraction, and the sign is what the next printed instruction reads ("If residential rental property or line 24 isn't more than line 26a, skip lines 26d and 26e"), so a negative value is the form's own answer and is printed as such.

Fact.Name: Date acquired for this Part III property (Form 4797 line 19 column (b))
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 19 column (b), the date this section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 property was acquired, printed in the property column (A through D) this collection item owns. It FEEDS THE ROUTING when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is unanswered: with both date columns entered, ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates derives the holding period (counted from the day after acquisition through the day of sale), which ../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete uses to send the non recapture remainder to Part I or Part II, and which releases the unanswered holding period loss refusal (../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss). An answered ../heldMoreThanOneYear still governs. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered leaves the printed cell blank, and then the holding period question must be answered for the item to complete.

Fact.Name: Date sold for this Part III property (Form 4797 line 19 column (c))
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 19 column (c), the date this section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 property was sold, printed in the property column (A through D) this collection item owns. It FEEDS THE ROUTING when ../heldMoreThanOneYear is unanswered: with both date columns entered, ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates derives the holding period (counted from the day after acquisition through the day of sale), which ../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete uses to send the non recapture remainder to Part I or Part II, and which releases the unanswered holding period loss refusal (../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss). An answered ../heldMoreThanOneYear still governs. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered leaves the printed cell blank, and then the holding period question must be answered for the item to complete.

Fact.Name: Calendar years between Part III line 19 column (b) and column (c)
Fact.Description: ../writableLineNineteenDateSold's year minus ../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired's year. An intermediate for ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates, reused by both its "more than one full calendar year apart" test and its "exactly one calendar year apart, so compare month and day" tie-break; the /form4797Section1231Sales/*/yearsBetweenAcquiredAndSold body over the Part III date columns. Only meaningful when both dates are answered; every reader reaches it only behind IsComplete guards on both dates.

Fact.Name: Held more than one year, computed from Part III line 19 columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableLineNineteenDateSold falls more than one full year after ../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired. IRC 1231(b)(1) admits depreciable and real trade or business property only when "held for more than 1 year", IRC 1222(3) draws the same line for a long-term gain, and the Instructions for Form 4797 give the count: begin counting on the day after you received the property and include the day you disposed of it. So a sale on the exact one-year anniversary of acquisition is held one year, not more, and routes to Part II; a sale one day later is held more than one year. THE GENERAL TEST ONLY. It stands in for ../heldMoreThanOneYear when that attestation is unanswered (../heldMoreThanOneYearComplete) and it releases the unanswered-holding loss refusal (../hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss). An attested-livestock item still routes on the section 1231(b)(3) month test (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet), not on this fact. Computed by calendar-date components rather than a fixed day count, so a February 29 acquisition is exact: more than one full year apart (the years differ by more than 1), OR exactly one year apart AND the sold month/day strictly later than the acquired month/day. The body is /form4797Section1231Sales/*/heldMoreThanOneYearByDates over the Part III date columns. Incomplete when either date is unanswered, which is why every reader tests both dates' IsComplete first.

Fact.Name: Held 12 months or more, computed from Part III line 19 columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableLineNineteenDateSold falls on or after the one-year anniversary of ../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired. IRC 1231(b)(3)(B) admits other livestock "held by him for 12 months or more from the date of acquisition", and the instructions count from the day after acquisition through the day of sale, so the anniversary date completes 12 months and qualifies, where ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates (more than 1 year) needs one day more. The ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates calendar-component body with the day comparison at or after rather than strictly after. A February 29 acquisition first qualifies on March 1 of a later non-leap year. The /form4797Section1231Sales twin over the Part III line 19 date columns; it derives the livestock holding test when ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths is unanswered (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet) and bounds the window in which an unanswered ../isLivestock can change the routing (../isLivestockComplete). Incomplete when either date is unanswered; read only behind both dates' IsComplete.

Fact.Name: Held 24 months or more, computed from Part III line 19 columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableLineNineteenDateSold falls on or after the two-year anniversary of ../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired: IRC 1231(b)(3)(A) admits cattle and horses "held by him for 24 months or more from the date of acquisition", counted as ../heldTwelveMonthsOrMoreByDates counts, so the anniversary date qualifies. The same body with the calendar-year difference compared against 2. The /form4797Section1231Sales twin over the Part III line 19 date columns; it derives the livestock holding test when ../writableLivestockHoldingMonths is unanswered (../livestockSection1231HoldingMet) and bounds the window in which an unanswered ../isLivestock can change the routing (../isLivestockComplete). Incomplete when either date is unanswered; read only behind both dates' IsComplete.

Fact.Name: Full years the farm land was held, computed from Part III line 19 columns (b) and (c) (the IRC 1252(a)(3) band index)
Fact.Description: The number of complete years of holding that ENDED BEFORE the day of sale, from ../writableLineNineteenDateAcquired and ../writableLineNineteenDateSold: the calendar-year difference (../yearsBetweenAcquiredAndSold), less one unless the sold month/day falls strictly after the acquired month/day, floored at 0. It indexes the same bands as ../writableFarmlandFullYearsHeld: 0 through 4 is "Within 5 years after the date it was acquired" (100 percent), 5 is "Within the sixth year" (80 percent), and so on to 9 or more (the tenth or later year, skip line 27). THE ANNIVERSARY DAY BELONGS TO THE EARLIER BAND. The instructions count a holding period from the day after acquisition through the day of disposal, so the fifth year runs through the fifth anniversary itself: land acquired on March 10 and sold on the fifth anniversary is disposed of within 5 years (100 percent); sold the next day, within the sixth year (80 percent). This is the same boundary ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates draws at one year. Read by ../farmlandFullYearsHeld only when ../writableFarmlandFullYearsHeld is unanswered and both dates are entered. Incomplete when either date is unanswered.

Fact.Name: Gross proceeds reported on Forms 1099-B or 1099-S (Form 4797 line 1a)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 line 1a, "Enter the gross proceeds from sales or exchanges reported to you for 2025 on Form(s) 1099-B or 1099-S (or substitute statement) that you are including on line 2, 10, or 20". A carry IN attestation, because nothing in this graph records WHICH dispositions a broker or a real estate reporting person reported to the IRS: /section1245Dispositions/*/grossSalesPrice is the sales price of every Part III disposition whether or not an information return was issued, so the printed figure is a strict subset the filer alone can identify. NON-NEGATIVE (gross proceeds), enforced by a Min 0 limit. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered means no such information return, and the box prints blank, which is what the form's own reconciliation posture expects. RECORD ONLY, and deliberately so: line 1a is a matching disclosure for the IRS, it is not an addend of line 7 or of any other printed total, so no fact in this graph reads it and no computed amount moves when it is answered.

Fact.Name: Gain included on lines 2, 10 and 24 from partial dispositions of MACRS assets (Form 4797 line 1b)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 line 1b, "Enter the total amount of gain that you are including on lines 2, 10, and 24 due to the partial dispositions of MACRS assets". A carry IN attestation: this graph models a disposition as the sale of a whole property and marks nothing as the partial disposition of a larger modified accelerated cost recovery system asset, so the split cannot be derived from /section1245Dispositions or from anything in form4684 or scheduleD. NON-NEGATIVE (the printed word is gain), enforced by a Min 0 limit. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered means the return reports no partial disposition and the box prints blank. RECORD ONLY: line 1b is a disclosure about amounts already counted elsewhere on the form, never a separate addend, so nothing in the graph reads it and no computed amount moves when it is answered.

Fact.Name: Loss included on lines 2 and 10 from partial dispositions of MACRS assets (Form 4797 line 1c)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 line 1c, "Enter the total amount of loss that you are including on lines 2 and 10 due to the partial dispositions of MACRS assets". The loss half of the line 1b disclosure and a carry IN for the same reason: nothing in this graph marks a disposition as the partial disposition of a larger MACRS asset. Entered as a POSITIVE amount, with a Min 0 limit, because the printed line asks for the total amount OF loss rather than a signed figure, exactly as line 1b asks for the total amount of gain. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered means no partial disposition and the box prints blank. RECORD ONLY: nothing in the graph reads it and no computed amount moves when it is answered.

Fact.Name: Ordinary gain from installment sales (Form 4797 Part II line 15, from Form 6252 line 25 or 36)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part II line 15, "Ordinary gain from installment sales from Form 6252, line 25 or 36" - the filer's own Form 6252 figure, entered as a carry IN attestation. The graph models Form 6252 (dictionary/ty2025/form6252.xml), and /form6252Sales/*/form4797Line15Amount carries its line 25 or 36 here; this entry is the line only on a return that files no Form 6252. The same posture as /writableSection1231GainFromInstallmentSales, which attests the SECTION 1231 slice of the same sale on Part I line 4; this is the ORDINARY recapture slice, and the two are different lines of Form 6252 (line 26 or 37 there, line 25 or 36 here). NON NEGATIVE, read off the form rather than chosen: the printed line says ordinary GAIN from installment sales with no "(loss)" branch, where line 16 one line below says "Ordinary gain or (loss)" - the internal contrast that settles it. A Min 0 Limit enforces it. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered means no installment sale, so /partIIOrdinaryGainFromInstallmentSales is 0 and every existing return is byte identical. FEEDS: /partIIOrdinaryGainFromInstallmentSales, an addend of line 17 (/partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen), which line 18b (/form4797OrdinaryIncome) carries to Schedule 1 line 4. READ ONLY when the return files no Form 6252: otherwise line 15 is read from the Form 6252 sales (/form6252Sales/*/form4797Line15Amount).

Fact.Name: Ordinary gain or (loss) from like kind exchanges (Form 4797 Part II line 16, from Form 8824)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part II line 16, "Ordinary gain or (loss) from like-kind exchanges from Form 8824" - the filer's own Form 8824 figure, entered as a carry IN attestation. The graph models Form 8824 (dictionary/ty2025/form8824.xml), and /form8824Exchanges/*/form4797Line16Amount carries its line 21 here; this entry is the line only on a return that files no Form 8824. It is the ORDINARY recapture recognized on the exchange, a different slice from the Part I line 5 section 1231 gain or loss of the same exchange. SIGNED: the printed line says "gain or (loss)", so no Min 0 Limit is written and a negative entry is a real ordinary deduction on line 17 - the same contrast that makes line 15 non negative. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered means no like kind exchange, so /partIIOrdinaryGainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges is 0 and every existing return is byte identical. FEEDS: /partIIOrdinaryGainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges, an addend of line 17 (/partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen), which line 18b (/form4797OrdinaryIncome) carries to Schedule 1 line 4. READ ONLY when the return files no Form 8824: otherwise line 16 is read from the Form 8824 exchanges (/form8824Exchanges/*/form4797Line16Amount).

Fact.Name: Section 179 expense deduction allowable in prior years (Form 4797 Part IV line 33, column (a))
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part IV line 33 column (a), "Section 179 expense deduction or depreciation allowable in prior years", for property whose business use dropped to 50% or less this year. A FILER SUPPLIED intake: the amount was deducted on a PRIOR year return, which this graph does not hold. Part IV is not a gain computation and has no column A through D property axis; it is one pair of columns, (a) section 179 and (b) section 280F(b)(2), so this is a return level scalar and not a collection leaf. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered leaves /partIVLine35Section179RecaptureAmount Result.Incomplete and the whole Part IV block prints blank, which is the correct paper outcome for the filer who has no business use drop to report.

Fact.Name: Depreciation allowable in prior years on listed property (Form 4797 Part IV line 33, column (b))
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part IV line 33 column (b), the section 280F(b)(2) column of "Section 179 expense deduction or depreciation allowable in prior years", for listed property whose qualified business use dropped to 50% or less this year. A FILER SUPPLIED intake: the depreciation was deducted on PRIOR year returns, which this graph does not hold. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered leaves /partIVLine35Section280FRecaptureAmount Result.Incomplete and the column prints blank.

Fact.Name: Recomputed depreciation, section 179 column (Form 4797 Part IV line 34, column (a))
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part IV line 34 column (a), "Recomputed depreciation": the depreciation that would have been allowable on the section 179 amount in the prior years had the property never been expensed, figured under the straight line method the instructions prescribe. A FILER SUPPLIED intake for the same reason line 33 is: it is a recomputation over PRIOR year facts this graph does not hold. ASKED WHEN: line 33 column (a) (/writablePartIVLine33Section179PriorDeduction) is answered; not asked otherwise, and the column then routes $0. REQUIRED once line 33 column (a) is answered: unanswered then leaves /partIVLine35Section179RecaptureAmount (printed blank) and /partIVLine35Section179RoutedAmount Incomplete, so /totalIncome is Incomplete and the return stops, because a recapture of unknown size is not zero. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0.

Fact.Name: Recomputed depreciation, section 280F(b)(2) column (Form 4797 Part IV line 34, column (b))
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part IV line 34 column (b), "Recomputed depreciation": the depreciation that would have been allowable on the listed property in the prior years under the straight line method section 280F(b)(1) imposes once qualified business use falls to 50% or less. A FILER SUPPLIED intake over PRIOR year facts this graph does not hold. ASKED WHEN: line 33 column (b) (/writablePartIVLine33Section280FPriorDepreciation) is answered; not asked otherwise, and the column then routes $0. REQUIRED once line 33 column (b) is answered: unanswered then leaves /partIVLine35Section280FRecaptureAmount (printed blank) and /partIVLine35Section280FRoutedAmount Incomplete, so /totalIncome is Incomplete and the return stops, because a recapture of unknown size is not zero. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min 0.

Fact.Name: Section 1231 gain or (loss) from like-kind exchanges from Form 8824 (Form 4797 line 5)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part I line 5, "Section 1231 gain or (loss) from like-kind exchanges from Form 8824" the filer's own Form 8824 figure, entered as a carry IN attestation. The graph models Form 8824 (dictionary/ty2025/form8824.xml), and /form8824Exchanges/*/form4797Line5Amount carries its line 22 here; this entry is the line only on a return that files no Form 8824. The same posture the module already takes at line 4 with /writableSection1231GainFromInstallmentSales and at line 8 with /writableNonrecapturedSection1231Loss. SIGNED, and the sign is read off the form rather than chosen: this line prints "gain or (loss)" where line 4 one line above prints "Section 1231 gain" with no loss branch, so no Min 0 limit is written here. OPTIONAL (three state): unanswered means the return reports no like kind exchange. FEEDS: the complete safe alias /section1231GainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges, an addend of Part I line 7 (/netSection1231GainOrLoss) in both of its arms. READ ONLY when the return files no Form 8824: otherwise line 5 is read from the Form 8824 exchanges (/form8824Exchanges/*/form4797Line5Amount).

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 dispositions
Fact.Description: The collection behind Form 4797 Part II line 10, one item per an ordinary gain or loss not already carried in on lines 11 through 16, which is where property held one year or less belongs. Distinct from /section1245Dispositions, which the dictionary defines as the Part III collection and whose items must attest exactly one of the printed section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 and 1255 classes; a Part II line 10 row is a disposition that carries none of those classes, so it has no home in that collection. The printed table has four rows, so the first four items print and a filer with more attaches a statement.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (g), gain or (loss)
Fact.Description: Column (g) for this row, the printed arithmetic verbatim: subtract column (f) from the sum of columns (d) and (e). May be positive or negative, and is not floored, because Part II line 10 carries losses as well as gains. CONSUMED: /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal is the complete safe CollectionSum of this leaf and is an addend of /partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen (line 17, "Combine lines 10 through 16"). The obligation this paragraph used to carry is discharged.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10, column (d) plus column (e)
Fact.Description: The sum of column (d) gross sales price and column (e) depreciation allowed or allowable, the intermediate the printed column (g) subtraction needs. Incomplete until both entries are answered, which leaves the printed column (g) cell blank rather than guessing a value.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (f)
Fact.Description: Column (f) of this Part II line 10 row: Cost or other basis, plus improvements and expense of sale. An intake leaf, because the graph holds no disposition of this kind at all. CONSUMED through ../gainOrLoss and /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal, which is an addend of /partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen (line 17, "Combine lines 10 through 16").

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (b)
Fact.Description: Column (b) of this Part II line 10 row: Date acquired (mo., day, yr.). QUESTION: "When did you acquire this property?" (a date). The column prints on the line 10 row and no fact reads it: whatever lands on line 10 is ordinary whatever its dates, so the graph runs no holding-period test on this table; that test runs on the Part I line 2 rows, where the dates decide the line. UNANSWERED: the printed cell is blank; no number changes.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (c)
Fact.Description: Column (c) of this Part II line 10 row: Date sold (mo., day, yr.). QUESTION: "When did you sell or otherwise dispose of this property?" (a date). The column prints on the line 10 row and no fact reads it: whatever lands on line 10 is ordinary whatever its dates, so the graph runs no holding-period test on this table; that test runs on the Part I line 2 rows, where the dates decide the line. UNANSWERED: the printed cell is blank; no number changes.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (e)
Fact.Description: Column (e) of this Part II line 10 row: Depreciation allowed or allowable since acquisition. An intake leaf, because the graph holds no disposition of this kind at all. CONSUMED through ../gainOrLoss and /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal, which is an addend of /partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen (line 17, "Combine lines 10 through 16").

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (a)
Fact.Description: Column (a) of this Part II line 10 row: Description of property. SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Describe the property." HELP TEXT: "Use this table for ordinary gains and losses: business property you held 1 year or less, and - however long you held it - property that is never section 1231 property: a patent, invention, model or design, secret formula or process, copyright, or literary, musical or artistic composition, letter or memorandum created by your own efforts (or received from its creator in a way that gave you the creator's basis, such as by gift); a U.S. Government publication you received other than by purchase at the normal sales price; inventory, or property held primarily for sale to customers; and property whose cost you deducted under the de minimis safe harbor for tangible property. None of these belongs in the Part I line 2 or Part III tables. An amount already reported as gross receipts on Schedule C or Schedule F is not entered again here." SOURCES: line 10 takes "ordinary gains and losses, not included on lines 11 through 16, including gains and losses from property held 1 year or less", and "If you receive ordinary income from a sale or other disposition of property and deducted the cost of the property under the tangible property de minimis safe harbor, report the income on line 10" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 8, left column); the chart sends de minimis property to Part II in BOTH holding-period columns (row 4, lines 40-42); the section 1231 exclusions are the bullets under "Transactions to which section 1231 does not apply" (lines 419-421 left, continuing at 358-377 right) and IRC 1231(b)(1)(A)-(D) (26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024, right column); Pub 544 states that a sale of property held mainly for sale to customers "is not a section 1231 transaction", that a self-created patent or copyright sale "results in ordinary income and is generally reported in Part II of Form 4797", and works a $1,000 machine expensed under the safe harbor and sold for $1,500: "you must report the $1,500 as ordinary gain on line 10 of Form 4797" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p544.pdf, page 41, left column). ASKED WHEN: once per row of the Part II line 10 table. UNANSWERED: the printed cell is blank; no number changes. VALIDATION: free text. WHAT IT FEEDS: the printed line 10 column (a) cell only; no fact reads it.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10 column (d)
Fact.Description: Column (d) of this Part II line 10 row: Gross sales price. An intake leaf, because the graph holds no disposition of this kind at all. CONSUMED through ../gainOrLoss and /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal, which is an addend of /partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen (line 17, "Combine lines 10 through 16").

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 dispositions
Fact.Description: The collection behind Form 4797 Part I line 2, one item per a section 1231 sale or exchange of property used in a trade or business, or an involuntary conversion from other than casualty or theft, held more than one year and carrying no depreciation recapture class. "Held more than one year" is TESTED from each row's own date columns (../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates), not assumed: a row held one year or less, or is carried to Part II line 10 (../routesToPartII), and a gain row with a date unanswered is unresolved until the date is entered. That is the GENERAL test only. LIVESTOCK held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes is the exception: IRC 1231(b)(3) and chart rows 7 and 8 test it at 24 months or more (cattle and horses) or 12 months or more (other livestock), not at more than 1 year (26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1). Each row asks ../writableIsLivestock (and, for livestock, ../writableIsCattleOrHorses), and ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriodByDates applies the month test to a row attested as livestock; an unanswered livestock question reads as not livestock. Distinct from /section1245Dispositions, which the dictionary defines as the Part III collection and whose items must attest exactly one of the printed section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 and 1255 classes; a Part I line 2 row is a disposition that carries none of those classes, so it has no home in that collection. The printed table has four rows, so the first four items print and a filer with more attaches a statement.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (g), gain or (loss)
Fact.Description: Column (g) for this row, the printed arithmetic verbatim: subtract column (f) from the sum of columns (d) and (e). May be positive or negative, and is not floored, because Part I line 2 carries losses as well as gains. CONSUMED: /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal is the complete safe CollectionSum of this leaf and is an addend of /netSection1231GainOrLoss (line 7, "Combine lines 2 through 6") in BOTH arms of that fact's Switch, so a filer whose whole Part I is a line 2 row now reports a line 7. The obligation this paragraph used to carry is discharged.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2, column (d) plus column (e)
Fact.Description: The sum of column (d) gross sales price and column (e) depreciation allowed or allowable, the intermediate the printed column (g) subtraction needs. Incomplete until both entries are answered, which leaves the printed column (g) cell blank rather than guessing a value.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (f)
Fact.Description: Column (f) of this Part I line 2 row: Cost or other basis, plus improvements and expense of sale. An intake leaf, because the graph holds no disposition of this kind at all. CONSUMED through ../gainOrLoss and /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal, which is an addend of /netSection1231GainOrLoss (line 7, "Combine lines 2 through 6").

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (b)
Fact.Description: Column (b) of this Part I line 2 row: Date acquired (mo., day, yr.). SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "When did you acquire this property?" (a date). HELP TEXT: "Your holding period begins the day after you acquired the property and includes the day you disposed of it. Property held 1 year or less belongs in the Part II line 10 table. Livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes stays in Part I only if held 24 months or more (cattle and horses) or 12 months or more (other livestock), counted the same way, so the anniversary qualifies." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 6, left column; the livestock month tests, lines 45-56). ASKED WHEN: every Part I line 2 row. UNANSWERED: a GAIN row with either date blank takes no default - its routing, the line 2 and line 10 totals and the return stay Incomplete until both dates are entered (../routesToPartII); a LOSS row with a date blank stays on line 2, where it is netted, the adverse-safe direction for a loss. With both dates answered and the row held more than one year, a row carrying column (e) depreciation and a gain refuses (../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain): it belongs in the Part III table. VALIDATION: a date. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../yearsBetweenAcquiredAndSold and ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates, hence ../routesToPartII and ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain, which splits column (g) between ../section1231Leg (Part I line 2, /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal) and ../partIIOrdinaryLeg (Part II line 10, /form4797Line2RowsRoutedToPartII); and the printed column (b) cell.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (c)
Fact.Description: Column (c) of this Part I line 2 row: Date sold (mo., day, yr.). SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "When did you sell or otherwise dispose of this property?" (a date). HELP TEXT: "Your holding period begins the day after you acquired the property and includes the day you disposed of it. Property held 1 year or less belongs in the Part II line 10 table. Livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes stays in Part I only if held 24 months or more (cattle and horses) or 12 months or more (other livestock), counted the same way, so the anniversary qualifies." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 6, left column; the livestock month tests, lines 45-56). ASKED WHEN: every Part I line 2 row. UNANSWERED: a GAIN row with either date blank takes no default - its routing, the line 2 and line 10 totals and the return stay Incomplete until both dates are entered (../routesToPartII); a LOSS row with a date blank stays on line 2, where it is netted, the adverse-safe direction for a loss. With both dates answered and the row held more than one year, a row carrying column (e) depreciation and a gain refuses (../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain): it belongs in the Part III table. VALIDATION: a date. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../yearsBetweenAcquiredAndSold and ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates, hence ../routesToPartII and ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain, which splits column (g) between ../section1231Leg (Part I line 2, /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal) and ../partIIOrdinaryLeg (Part II line 10, /form4797Line2RowsRoutedToPartII); and the printed column (c) cell.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (e)
Fact.Description: Column (e) of this Part I line 2 row: Depreciation allowed or allowable since acquisition. Read by ../grossSalesPricePlusDepreciation, hence ../gainOrLoss and /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal (an addend of /netSection1231GainOrLoss, line 7), and by ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain: a row held more than one year that carries depreciation here and shows a gain is a Part III case and refuses until it is re-entered in the Part III table. Land carries no depreciation, so its answer is zero.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (a)
Fact.Description: Column (a) of this Part I line 2 row: Description of property. SCREEN SPEC - this is the screen that decides which table a disposition belongs in. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Describe the property (for example, 'Parcel of land, 5 acres')." HELP TEXT: "Use this table for property you used in your trade or business and held MORE than 1 year that is not section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 property: most often bare land, and the LAND half of a sale of a building together with its land. Split such a sale - report the building in the Part III table and the land here. A depreciated building, machine or vehicle sold at a GAIN belongs in the Part III table, which computes its depreciation recapture. Property you held 1 year or less belongs in the Part II line 10 table. Livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes may be entered here: answer the livestock questions on this row. An animal you bought and depreciated and are selling at a gain after its holding period belongs in the Part III table." The split rule is the instructions' own ("For example, for property held more than 1 year, report the sale of a building in Part III and the land in Part I", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 2, right column); the table routing is the "Where To Make First Entry" chart, rows 1a and 2a (a depreciable property sold at a gain and held more than 1 year goes to Part III) and row 5 (other farmland held more than 1 year goes to Part I), https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1. LIVESTOCK: the row asks ../writableIsLivestock and ../writableIsCattleOrHorses and routes on the IRC 1231(b)(3) month test (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1), so a raised animal's gain prints in Part I as chart rows 7c and 8c require. ASKED WHEN: once per row of the Part I line 2 table. UNANSWERED: the printed cell is blank; no number changes. VALIDATION: free text. WHAT IT FEEDS: the printed line 2 column (a) cell only; no fact reads it. A row typed here anyway whose dates show 1 year or less is carried to Part II line 10 by ../routesToPartII; a depreciated property sold at a gain after more than 1 year refuses (../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain, legible through /hasRefusedForm4797Line2Row) until it is re-entered in the Part III table.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2 column (d)
Fact.Description: Column (d) of this Part I line 2 row: Gross sales price. An intake leaf, because the graph holds no disposition of this kind at all. CONSUMED through ../gainOrLoss and /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal, which is an addend of /netSection1231GainOrLoss (line 7, "Combine lines 2 through 6").

Fact.Name: Calendar years between column (b) and column (c)
Fact.Description: ../writableDateSold's year minus ../writableDateAcquired's year. An intermediate for ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates, reused by both its "more than one full calendar year apart" test and its "exactly one calendar year apart, so compare month and day" tie-break. Only meaningful when both dates are answered; every reader reaches it only behind IsComplete guards on both dates, so an unanswered date here never has to resolve.

Fact.Name: Held more than one year, computed from columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableDateSold falls more than one full year after ../writableDateAcquired. IRC 1231(b)(1) admits only property held for more than 1 year, and the Instructions for Form 4797 give the count: begin counting on the day after you received the property and include the day you disposed of it. So a sale on the exact one-year anniversary of acquisition is held one year, not more; a sale one day later is held more than one year. THIS IS THE GENERAL TEST, the one chart rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 use. LIVESTOCK held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes is the exception: IRC 1231(b)(3) and chart rows 7 and 8 test it at 24 months or more (cattle and horses) or 12 months or more (other livestock), not at more than 1 year (26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1), so on a row attested as livestock ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriodByDates reads the month test instead of this fact. Computed by calendar-date components rather than a fixed day count, so a February 29 acquisition is exact: more than one full year apart (the years differ by more than 1), OR exactly one year apart AND the sold month/day strictly later than the acquired month/day. The body is scheduleD:/form8949Transactions/*/heldMoreThanOneYearByDates verbatim, which applies the same day-after rule to Form 8949. Incomplete when either date is unanswered (its /year accessor has nothing to read), which is why every reader tests both dates' IsComplete first.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 row is livestock held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "Is this property livestock (cattle, horses or other livestock, but not poultry) that you held for draft, breeding, dairy or sporting purposes?" (Yes or No). HELP TEXT: "Livestock held for these purposes counts as trade or business property in Part I only if you held it 24 months or more (cattle and horses) or 12 months or more (other livestock), counted from the day after you acquired it through the day you sold it. Poultry, chickens, turkeys, pigeons, geese, other birds, fish, frogs and reptiles are not livestock. An animal you bought and depreciated and are selling at a gain after that holding period belongs in the Part III table, which figures its depreciation recapture." (IRC 1231(b)(3), 26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024, right column; the chart rows 7 and 8, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1; the livestock paragraphs and note, lines 392-403, left column). ASKED WHEN: every Part I line 2 row. UNANSWERED: read as NOT livestock, so the row takes the general more-than-1-year test from its dates: the additivity posture /section1245Dispositions/*/isLivestock takes on the Part III table, which keeps every return that never sees this question resolving unchanged. A genuinely livestock row left unanswered is routed by the general test, which differs from the month test for other livestock sold on the 12-month anniversary and for cattle and horses held 13 to 23 months (disclosed). VALIDATION: Boolean. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriodByDates, hence ../routesToPartII (Part I line 2 or Part II line 10) and ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain (the Part III refusal).

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 livestock row is cattle or horses (the 24-month test, not the 12-month one)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION: "Is this animal cattle or a horse?" (Yes or No). HELP TEXT: "Cattle and horses must be held 24 months or more to be reported in Part I; other livestock, 12 months or more." (IRC 1231(b)(3)(A) and (B), 26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024, right column; chart rows 7 and 8, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1). ASKED WHEN: this row's ../writableIsLivestock is answered Yes; nothing reads it on any other row. UNANSWERED on a livestock row: the threshold follows the row's sign (../appliesCattleOrHorseThreshold): a GAIN is tested at 24 months and a LOSS at 12 months, each the adverse-safe direction, the posture this table already takes for an unanswered date (../routesToPartII). VALIDATION: Boolean. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../appliesCattleOrHorseThreshold, hence ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriodByDates.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 livestock row is measured at 24 months (cattle and horses, or an unanswered class on a gain)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsCattleOrHorses when answered. When it is unanswered, TRUE for a gain (column (g) above zero) and FALSE otherwise, so an unattested class tests a gain at the longer 24-month threshold (sending a 12 to 23 month gain to Part II ordinary rather than to section 1231) and a loss at the shorter 12-month one (keeping a 12 to 23 month loss in the section 1231 netting and the section 1231(c) lookback rather than deducting it as ordinary). Each default is the adverse-safe direction for its sign, which is why no refusal is needed. Incomplete only when the class is unanswered and column (g) cannot be computed. Read only on a row whose ../writableIsLivestock is answered true.

Fact.Name: Held 12 months or more, computed from columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableDateSold falls on or after the one-year anniversary of ../writableDateAcquired. IRC 1231(b)(3)(B) admits other livestock "held by him for 12 months or more from the date of acquisition", and the instructions count from the day after acquisition through the day of sale, so the anniversary date completes 12 months and qualifies, where ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates (more than 1 year) needs one day more. The ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates calendar-component body with the day comparison at or after rather than strictly after. A February 29 acquisition first qualifies on March 1 of a later non-leap year. Incomplete when either date is unanswered; read only behind both dates' IsComplete.

Fact.Name: Held 24 months or more, computed from columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: TRUE when ../writableDateSold falls on or after the two-year anniversary of ../writableDateAcquired: IRC 1231(b)(3)(A) admits cattle and horses "held by him for 24 months or more from the date of acquisition", counted as ../heldTwelveMonthsOrMoreByDates counts, so the anniversary date qualifies. The same body with the calendar-year difference compared against 2. Incomplete when either date is unanswered; read only behind both dates' IsComplete.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 row meets its section 1231 holding period, from columns (b) and (c)
Fact.Description: The holding test this row is measured by, with both dates answered. A row attested as livestock (../writableIsLivestock true) takes the IRC 1231(b)(3) month test: ../heldTwentyFourMonthsOrMoreByDates when ../appliesCattleOrHorseThreshold is true (cattle and horses), else ../heldTwelveMonthsOrMoreByDates (other livestock). Every other row, including one whose livestock question is unanswered, takes the general test, ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates. The single reader of the holding period for both ../routesToPartII and ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain, so the two never disagree about a row. Incomplete when a livestock row's threshold cannot be chosen (class unanswered and column (g) not computable); read only behind both dates' IsComplete.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 row routed to Part II line 10 (held one year or less; unresolved for a gain with a date unanswered)
Fact.Description: TRUE when this row belongs on Part II line 10 rather than Part I line 2. With BOTH dates answered it is the negation of ../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriodByDates: a row held one year or less (or a livestock row under its 24 or 12 month threshold) goes to Part II whatever its sign, as the "Where To Make First Entry" chart's column (b) prints for rows 1, 2, 3 and 5, and IRC 1231(b)(1) admits only property held more than one year. With EITHER date unanswered: FALSE for a LOSS or a zero (column (g) not above zero), and for a GAIN NOTHING - the Switch has no default case and runs off the end, so this fact, the row's legs, the line 2 and line 10 totals and the return stay Incomplete until both dates are entered. WHY NO DEFAULT FOR A GAIN. Staying on line 2 would grant section 1231 treatment (a net section 1231 gain leaves at long-term capital gain rates through /section1231LtcgPortion) that the dates were never entered to show, and Part II would silently tax a long-held gain at ordinary rates; the chart prints no third branch, and the holding period is always knowable from the dates the filer holds. The Part III table takes the same posture (/section1245Dispositions/*/heldMoreThanOneYearComplete). For a LOSS, staying on line 2 IS the adverse direction: it offsets section 1231 gains that would otherwise leave at long-term rates, and it enters the section 1231(c) nonrecaptured-loss pool through /nonrecapturedSection1231Loss - so an unanswered-date loss stays where the filer typed it and needs no refusal. /section1245Dispositions/*/hasUnansweredHoldingPeriodLoss refuses only because ITS default is Part II. LIVESTOCK: for a row attested as livestock (../writableIsLivestock) the dated test is the IRC 1231(b)(3) month test, 24 months or more for cattle and horses and 12 months or more for other livestock, the anniversary qualifying (26 U.S.C. 1231, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1231&num=0&edition=2024; https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 1). Chart rows 7 and 8 send a livestock row under its threshold to Part II whatever its sign and one at or past it to Part I, so a raised animal's gain stays on line 2 as rows 7c and 8c print it. SHAPE: a Switch whose first When reads only the two IsCompletes, never a bare All or Any over ../heldMoreThanOneYearByDates, which is Incomplete whenever a date is blank. This fact is Incomplete when a date is blank AND column (g) is a gain or cannot be computed. PRINT RESIDUE: a routed row still prints in the Part I line 2 table, because the printed-form register binds the first four /form4797Section1231Sales rows there. The screen cue on ../writableDescription is the primary instrument (a short-held row belongs in /form4797OrdinaryDispositions); this routing is the safety net for the tax.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 row is a depreciated property sold at a gain after more than one year (a Part III case typed into Part I; refusal gate)
Fact.Description: TRUE when this row's dates are BOTH answered and show it held past its section 1231 holding period (../meetsSection1231HoldingPeriodByDates: more than one year, or for a row attested as livestock 24 or 12 months or more), AND column (e) depreciation is above zero, AND column (g) is a GAIN. That population is exactly the "Where To Make First Entry" chart's rows 1a, 2a, 7a and 8a in column (c): depreciable tangible or real trade or business property, or purchased livestock, sold at a gain after its holding period goes to Part III (1245) or Part III (1250), never to a Part I line 2 row. A livestock row under its threshold goes to Part II through ../routesToPartII instead and is not refused here. IRC 1245(a)(1) and 1250(a)(1) treat such a gain as ordinary income to the extent of the recapture those sections define, and this table carries no property class to compute it, so taking the whole gain as a section 1231 gain on line 2 is an under-charge this graph cannot price. The refusal is therefore the only instrument: ../section1231Leg has no arm for this row, so it, /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal, /netSection1231GainOrLoss and /totalIncome resolve Incomplete, and /hasRefusedForm4797Line2Row makes the refusal legible. THE REMEDY is to re-enter the property in the Part III table (/section1245Dispositions) with its section 1245 or section 1250 class, where its recapture is computed; if it is land, its column (e) is zero and it computes here. OUTSIDE THE POPULATION, by construction: a depreciated row sold at a LOSS stays on line 2 and computes (chart rows 1b and 2b, column (c), send it to Part I; recapture needs a gain); an undepreciated row computes; and a depreciated GAIN row with a date unanswered is FALSE here because ../routesToPartII leaves it unresolved (Incomplete) until the date is entered, and the dated answer then decides between this refusal and Part II. COMPLETE-SAFETY: a Switch whose first When reads only the two dates' IsCompletes, the ../routesToPartII shape, so a blank date resolves Complete false rather than collapsing the gate; it reads only the row's own writables and per-row arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Refused Part I line 2 rows (a depreciated property sold at a gain after more than one year)
Fact.Description: The sub-collection of /form4797Section1231Sales whose ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain is true: rows that belong in the Part III table and refuse here. Used to compute the return-level flag /hasRefusedForm4797Line2Row; the /section1245DispositionsUnsupported Filter shape.

Fact.Name: Return has a refused Form 4797 Part I line 2 row (a depreciated property sold at a gain after more than one year)
Fact.Description: True when any Part I line 2 row has BOTH dates answered and held more than one year, depreciation above zero in column (e), and a gain in column (g) (/form4797Section1231Sales/*/hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain). Such a row is a Part III case: its gain is subject to section 1245 or section 1250 recapture this table cannot compute, so /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal, /netSection1231GainOrLoss and /totalIncome resolve Result.Incomplete (the return refuses to complete) and this flag makes the refusal legible. THE REMEDY the application shows: move the property to the Part III table and answer its section 1245 or section 1250 class there. Complete false on every return that never creates the Part I line 2 collection, and on every return with no such row. It reports DECIDED refusals only: a row whose ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain cannot yet be decided (both dates answered and held more than one year, but column (e) or column (g) blank) leaves the Filter Incomplete and this flag Complete false, while that row's own leg and line 7 are Incomplete.

Fact.Name: This row's Part I line 2 amount (column (g) when the row stays on line 2)
Fact.Description: Column (g) of this row when it stays on Part I line 2 (../routesToPartII false) and is not a depreciated property sold at a gain after more than one year (../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain false); $0 when it is routed to Part II line 10. The summand of /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal. NO default arm, deliberately, so the third state is Result.Incomplete: a row that ../hasDepreciationOnLongHeldGain flags is a Part III case whose recapture this table cannot compute, and it refuses (legible through /hasRefusedForm4797Line2Row) rather than computing its whole gain as section 1231. The same missing default makes an undecidable ../routesToPartII (a date blank and column (g) not computable) Incomplete, never a guessed or placeholder $0.

Fact.Name: This row's Part II line 10 amount (column (g) when the row is routed to Part II)
Fact.Description: Column (g) of this row when ../routesToPartII is true - a row held one year or less - else $0; a gain row with a date unanswered has an undecided route and this leg is Incomplete. Summed by /form4797Line2RowsRoutedToPartII onto Part II line 10, where it is ordinary whatever its sign. Two mutually exclusive cases and NO default, so an undecidable route is Incomplete rather than a placeholder $0 on line 10.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 rows routed to Part II line 10 (complete safe)
Fact.Description: CollectionSum of /form4797Section1231Sales/*/partIIOrdinaryLeg when the Part I line 2 collection has been created, else $0: the column (g) amounts of the rows the graph moves from line 2 to line 10 because they were held one year or less, or are gains with a date unanswered. A second term of /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal, which is the ONE wiring site: line 17 (/partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen), /schedule1Line4Form4797Leg and, through line 17, /form4797OrdinaryIncome all read that total and inherit this term. Gated on IsComplete of the collection for the reasons /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal gives.

Fact.Name: Part I line 2 rows that print on line 2 (the rows the graph keeps on line 2)
Fact.Description: The sub-collection of /form4797Section1231Sales whose ../routesToPartII is false: the rows whose column (g) is summed into /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal and so into line 7. The printed Part I line 2 table binds to THIS collection rather than to the whole /form4797Section1231Sales, so a row the graph carries to Part II line 10 (held one year or less) does not print on line 2 while its amount is absent from line 7, and the printed line 2 rows foot to line 7's line 2 term. A refused row (a depreciated long-held gain) stays in this collection and keeps printing; the return is Incomplete anyway. A row whose route cannot be decided leaves this collection Incomplete. The first four items print; a filer with more attaches a statement. The routed rows' print on line 10 is a separate, unbuilt print step.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part I line 2, column (g) total of the rows that stay on line 2 (complete safe)
Fact.Description:
Round(CollectionSum(/form4797Section1231Sales/*/section1231Leg)) when the Part I line 2 collection has been created, else $0: the Part I line 2 rows the filer types, carried to the printed line 7 combine. A row the graph routes to Part II line 10 (held one year or less, see /form4797Section1231Sales/*/routesToPartII) contributes $0 here; a gain row with a date unanswered has no decided route and leaves this total Incomplete and its column (g) to /form4797Line2RowsRoutedToPartII instead.
GATED ON IsComplete OF THE COLLECTION ITSELF, not on /claimsSection1245Disposition. The line 2 collection is a different collection from /section1245Dispositions and a filer can populate either without the other; a bare CollectionSum over a collection that was never created resolves Incomplete, which would carry an Incomplete onto line 7 for every return that has no Form 4797 at all. This is the shape /farmLivestockGainsFromForm4797 uses over its own collection, with the collection's own answered ness standing in for the claims Bool this collection does not have. A CREATED BUT EMPTY collection reads as answered and sums to $0, which is the same answer the unanswered arm gives, so the two arms agree wherever they can both be reached.
A HALF ANSWERED ROW STILL LEAVES THIS INCOMPLETE, deliberately: /form4797Section1231Sales/*/grossSalesPricePlusDepreciation is Incomplete until both column (d) and column (e) are answered, so a partly typed row's ../section1231Leg is Incomplete (never a silent $0) and the CollectionSum over it does not resolve. That is the module's stance on a combine line whose own inputs are blank; the printed cell is blank too.
THE ADDEND SITS OUTSIDE THE /claimsSection1245Disposition GATE in /netSection1231GainOrLoss for the reason /casualtyGainFromForm4684 and /section1231GainFromInstallmentSales each give in their own Descriptions: a filer whose only Part I amount is a line 2 row has no /section1245Dispositions item at all, so an addend inside that gate would leave exactly that population at $0.

Fact.Name: Form 4797 Part II line 10, column (g) total: the typed line 10 rows plus the Part I line 2 rows routed to Part II (complete safe)
Fact.Description:
Round of TWO terms: CollectionSum(/form4797OrdinaryDispositions/*/gainOrLoss) when the Part II line 10 collection has been created, else $0 - the typed line 10 rows - plus /form4797Line2RowsRoutedToPartII, the Part I line 2 rows the graph routes to line 10 because they were held one year or less (or are gains with a date unanswered). This is the ONE wiring site for those routed rows: the printed line 17 combine ("Combine lines 10 through 16", /partIIOrdinaryCombineLineSeventeen), /schedule1Line4Form4797Leg and, through line 17, /form4797OrdinaryIncome all read this fact and inherit both terms. The routed rows come from /form4797Section1231Sales, which is disjoint from /section1245Dispositions by its own definition, so they are no double count of /partIISection1245Ordinary either. An UNDECIDABLE Part I line 2 row (a date blank and column (g) not computable) leaves the routed term, and so this total, line 17, /schedule1Line4Form4797Leg and /form4797OrdinaryIncome, Incomplete; line 7 is Incomplete for that return already, so no return that completed stops completing.
TWO DIFFERENT LINE 10 QUANTITIES, BOTH PRINTED ON LINE 10, AND BOTH ARE ADDENDS. The printed line 10 table is one table: /partIISection1245Ordinary carries the /section1245Dispositions items that failed their own holding period and therefore print in that table, and this fact carries the /form4797OrdinaryDispositions rows, which are dispositions with no section 1245, 1250, 1252, 1254 or 1255 class and so have no home in the Part III collection at all. The two collections are disjoint by construction, which is what makes adding both a sum rather than a double count.
GATED ON IsComplete OF THE COLLECTION ITSELF and complete safe for the same reasons its Part I twin /form4797Line2Section1231SalesTotal gives; see that fact's Description.

Fact.Name: The Form 4797 part of Schedule 1 line 4
Fact.Description: The Form 4797 part of the Schedule 1 (Form 1040) line 4 amount: the SIX addends of the printed Form 4797 line 17 ("Combine lines 10 through 16") that Form 4797 itself contributes. /partIISection1245Ordinary and /form4797Line10OrdinaryDispositionsTotal are the two halves of the printed line 10 table - the Part III dispositions that failed their own holding period, and the typed Part II line 10 rows together with the Part I line 2 rows the graph routes to line 10 - and the collections are disjoint by construction, so adding both is a sum rather than a double count. /section1231RecharacterizedOrdinary is lines 11 and 12, /section1245OrdinaryRecapture is line 13 (the Part III line 31 recapture), /partIIOrdinaryGainFromInstallmentSales is line 15 and /partIIOrdinaryGainOrLossFromLikeKindExchanges is line 16. TWO TERMS OF THE PRINTED LINE 4 AMOUNT ARE DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED, and both are Form 4684 quantities that drive the OTHER line 4 checkbox: the line 14 leg /casualtyOrTheftNetGainOrLoss, and the line 18a add-back /lossFromForm4684ColumnBiiOnLineEleven, which can only ever cancel part of that leg. This fact is therefore NOT the printed line 4 figure - that is /form4797OrdinaryIncome (line 18b) - and it is read only by the two nonzero tests /hasSchedule1Line4Form4797Gain and /hasSchedule1Line4Form4797Loss. May be a net loss.

Fact.Name: Additional depreciation after 1969 and before 1976, complete-safe (Form 4797 Part III line 26d, printed cell)
Fact.Description: ../writableAdditionalDepreciation1969To1975 when answered, else $0 - the IsComplete/Switch pattern, the ../additionalDepreciationAfter1975 idiom verbatim. THIS IS THE PRINTED LINE 26d CELL: the printed-form register maps Part III columns A-D to /section1245Dispositions/[0..3]/additionalDepreciation1969To1975, exactly as line 26a is mapped to ../additionalDepreciationAfter1975. Complete-safe so an item nobody had any reason to answer this on resolves Complete $0 instead of spreading an Incomplete into line 26e.

Fact.Name: Property is residential rental property (Form 4797 Part III line 26c skip rule, carry-IN)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "Was this building residential rental property?" HELP TEXT: "Residential rental property is a building where at least 80% of the gross rental income is rental income from dwelling units - an apartment house, a rented house or duplex, and the like. A hotel, motel or other establishment where more than half the units are used on a transient basis is NOT residential rental property. Answer No for an office, a store, a warehouse, a factory or any other commercial building." WHY IT IS ASKED: Form 4797 Part III line 26c ends "If residential rental property or line 24 isn't more than line 26a, skip lines 26d and 26e" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f4797.pdf, page 2). That skip rule is a DISJUNCTION and only the second arm can be read off the arithmetic, so the first arm needs this answer. The statutory reason is IRC 1250(a)(2)(B)(iii): the applicable percentage on the 1970-1975 depreciation slice falls to zero once residential rental property has been held 200 full months, and any property placed in service before 1976 and still held in TY2025 is far past that. ASKED WHEN: the disposition attests ../isSection1250Property TRUE and the filer has entered a POSITIVE Form 4797 line 26d amount in ../writableAdditionalDepreciation1969To1975 whose line 26c is also positive - that band is the only place the answer changes a number, and it is the same screen the line 26d amount is entered on. UNANSWERED: REFUSED inside that band. ../hasUnansweredResidentialRentalOnLine26d takes the item out of ../isInScope, /hasUnsupportedSection1245Disposition goes true and the return refuses to complete rather than guessing. Guessing either way is wrong in a named direction: assuming NOT residential over-recaptures a residential filer, and assuming residential under-recaptures nonresidential 1969-1975 property, whose applicable percentage is 100% under IRC 1250(a)(2)(B)(v). Outside the band the question is never asked and its absence reads as No through ../isResidentialRentalPropertyComplete, which changes nothing because line 26e is zero on either reading there. VALIDATION: Boolean, Yes / No, no default, no Min or Max. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../section1250Line26e (the printed line 26e cell), hence line 26g, Part III line 31, Form 4797 line 13, line 17 and Schedule 1 line 4; and inversely the 25%-capped unrecaptured section 1250 gain group, which is measured net of the ordinary recapture this cell carries.

Fact.Name: Residential rental property attestation (complete-safe)
Fact.Description: ../writableIsResidentialRentalProperty when answered, else false (the IsComplete/Switch pattern, the ../isSection1250PropertyComplete idiom verbatim). Unanswered reads as NOT residential rental, which is the reading that leaves an item exactly where it stood before this pair existed. THAT DEFAULT IS ONLY EVER REACHED OUTSIDE THE BAND WHERE IT WOULD MATTER, and that is what makes it safe rather than convenient: ../hasUnansweredResidentialRentalOnLine26d refuses the item whenever line 26c and line 26d are both positive and this attestation is unanswered, so the false tail here is reached only where line 26e is zero on either reading.

Fact.Name: Unanswered residential-rental attestation on a live line 26d (refusal gate)
Fact.Description: The sibling of ../hasUnansweredAdditionalDepreciationGain, and the price of building the first arm of the printed line 26c skip rule. True when the item is attested section 1250 real property, the raw smaller-of line 26c and line 26d (../section1250Line26eSmallerOfLine26cOr26d) is POSITIVE, and ../writableIsResidentialRentalProperty is UNANSWERED. Such an item REFUSES via ../isInScope. THE BAND IS EXACTLY WHERE THE TWO READINGS DIFFER, which is why the gate is this narrow. A positive raw minimum means line 26c and line 26d are BOTH positive; on residential rental property the form skips lines 26d and 26e and line 26e is $0, and on any other section 1250 property line 26e is that positive minimum. Everywhere else - line 26d unanswered or zero, a loss or zero-gain item, line 24 not more than line 26a - line 26e is $0 under both readings and the attestation cannot move a number, so the item is not held back. NEITHER DEFAULT IS AVAILABLE, and naming both directions is the argument. Reading unanswered as NOT residential over-recaptures a residential filer and strips the same dollars out of the 25%-capped unrecaptured section 1250 group; reading it as residential under-recaptures nonresidential 1969-1975 property, whose applicable percentage is 100% under IRC 1250(a)(2)(B)(v). A refusal is the only answer that is never a wrong number. COMPLETE-SAFETY: this gate reads only the item's OWN facts - one completeness test on ../writableIsResidentialRentalProperty, one wrapper over ../isSection1250Property, and the raw line 26e helper, which is per-item arithmetic over ../totalGain and the two additional depreciation intakes - and never a flow-derived fact, so it cannot cascade an Incomplete into a return without this item. Complete-FALSE on every return that reports no section 1250 disposition with a positive line 26d, which is every committed scenario.

Fact.Name: The smaller of line 26c or line 26d, with the printed skip rule applied (Form 4797 Part III line 26e, printed cell)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 26e for this property, "Enter the smaller of line 26c or 26d", with the printed skip rule applied to BOTH its arms. Line 26c ends "If residential rental property or line 24 isn't more than line 26a, skip lines 26d and 26e", and a skipped cell is blank, which is $0 downstream. THE RULE IS A DISJUNCTION AND EACH ARM HAS ITS OWN CARRIER. Arm one is ../isResidentialRentalPropertyComplete, the filer's attestation: a residential rental building skips the pair outright and this cell is $0 however large line 26c and line 26d are. Arm two is the floor at zero: "line 24 isn't more than line 26a" is exactly the case in which line 26c is zero or negative, and line 26d is non-negative, so flooring the raw minimum ../section1250Line26eSmallerOfLine26cOr26d at zero reproduces it. NEITHER ARM MAY BE GUESSED. An item whose line 26c and line 26d are both positive and whose residential-rental attestation is unanswered is REFUSED by ../hasUnansweredResidentialRentalOnLine26d through ../isInScope, because a silent default would over-recapture a residential filer or under-recapture nonresidential 1969-1975 property, whose applicable percentage is 100% under IRC 1250(a)(2)(B)(v). TAX-AFFECTING, NOT PRINT-ONLY: ../section1250OrdinaryRecaptureContribution (line 26g) adds this cell to lines 26b and 26f, so it flows line 26g to line 31 to Form 4797 line 13 and on to Schedule 1 line 4, and the same dollars are stripped out of the 25%-capped unrecaptured section 1250 group by /unrecapturedSection1250GainComponent. VALUE NEUTRAL where line 26d is unanswered, which is the whole TY2025 population outside pre-1976 property: line 26d reads $0, the raw minimum is then non-positive, and this cell is $0 on either arm.

Fact.Name: The smaller of line 26c or line 26d, ungated (Form 4797 Part III line 26e, helper)
Fact.Description: The arithmetic of Form 4797 Part III line 26e, "Enter the smaller of line 26c or 26d", before the printed skip rule: LesserOf(../section1250Line26c, ../additionalDepreciation1969To1975). A HELPER, not the printed cell - ../section1250Line26e is the printed cell and applies the floor this fact deliberately does not. ../section1250Line26c is NOT floored at zero (its own description says so: "a negative value is the form's own answer and is printed as such"), so this raw minimum can be negative, which is precisely the case the printed skip rule disposes of.

Fact.Name: Section 291 amount, structurally zero on an individual return (Form 4797 Part III line 26f, printed cell)
Fact.Description: Form 4797 Part III line 26f, "Section 291 amount (corporations only)", for this property. A STRUCTURAL $0 AND NOT AN INTAKE: the printed caption limits the box to corporations and this dictionary files individual returns, and the instructions for line 26f describe it as "The amount the corporation treats as ordinary income under section 291". Nothing on an individual return can supply a value, so the cell is the module zero and the graph says so once, in the printed cell, rather than leaving the box unmapped. Deliberately per-item rather than a scalar so the printed columns follow /section1245Dispositions and columns with no disposition stay blank. Line 26g (../section1250OrdinaryRecaptureContribution) adds line 26b, line 26e and THIS FACT, so it reads its three printed terms rather than a literal. Because this fact is a structural zero the rewire changes no number.

Fact.Name: Additional depreciation after 1969 and before 1976 (Form 4797 Part III line 26d, carry-IN)
Fact.Description: SCREEN SPEC. QUESTION, as it should be asked: "How much additional depreciation did you take on this property after 1969 and before 1976?" HELP TEXT: "Additional depreciation is the amount by which the depreciation you actually took exceeds what straight line depreciation would have been for the same period. Enter the figure for 1970 through 1975 only. IF STRAIGHT LINE DEPRECIATION FOR THE PERIOD AFTER 1975 EXCEEDS THE ACTUAL DEPRECIATION YOU TOOK FOR THAT LATER PERIOD, REDUCE THIS AMOUNT BY THE EXCESS. Do not enter less than zero." (2025 Instructions for Form 4797, Line 26d: "Enter the additional depreciation after 1969 and before 1976. If straight line depreciation exceeds the actual depreciation for the period after 1975, reduce line 26d by the excess. Do not enter less than zero on line 26d." - https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i4797.pdf, page 11.) THE POST-1975 REDUCTION IS PART OF THIS ANSWER AND NOT A SEPARATE FACT, and that is a DECISION rather than an omission: the graph holds no per-period depreciation history at all, so it can neither compute the excess nor check the filer's arithmetic. The filer states the net figure, which is what the printed cell asks for. ASKED WHEN: the disposition attests ../isSection1250Property TRUE and the property was placed in service before 1976. A POSITIVE answer also makes ../writableIsResidentialRentalProperty required, because the printed line 26c skip rule turns on it; the two belong on one screen. UNANSWERED: DEFAULTED to $0 through ../additionalDepreciation1969To1975, which is the right reading for the overwhelming majority of TY2025 dispositions, whose property was placed in service after 1975. A $0 line 26d makes line 26e $0 on either arm of the skip rule, so the default can never move a number on its own. VALIDATION: Dollar, Min $0 (declared Limit) - the instructions say "Do not enter less than zero on line 26d". No Max. WHAT THE ANSWER FEEDS: ../additionalDepreciation1969To1975, the printed line 26d cell, then line 26e, line 26g, Part III line 31, Form 4797 line 13 and Schedule 1 line 4. THE POPULATION IS SMALL BUT NOT EMPTY: section 1250 property acquired in 1970-1975 and still held is fifty years old and can be disposed of in TY2025, which is why the IRS still prints the line and why its XFA widget is fillable (no access="readOnly").

Fact.Name: Form 1099-S VOID box

Fact.Name: Form 1099-S box 1, date of closing
Fact.Description: Form 1099-S box 1, "Date of closing" — the form's own transferor instruction reads "Box 1. Shows the date of closing." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099s--2025.pdf, page 4). Fact.Name: Form 1099-S box 2, gross proceeds
Fact.Description: Form 1099-S box 2, "Gross proceeds", as printed on THIS form. Gross proceeds include cash and notes payable to you, notes assumed by the transferee (buyer), and any notes paid off at settlement. Fact.Name: Form 1099-S box 4, transferor received property or services
Fact.Description: Form 1099-S box 4, "Check here if the transferor received or will receive property or services as part of the consideration" (Copy A wording, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099s--2025.pdf, page 2; Copy B prints it as "Transferor received or will receive property or services as part of the consideration (if checked)", lines 58-59). The form's own transferor instruction: "If checked, shows that you received or will receive services or property (other than cash or notes) as part of the consideration for the property transferred. The value of any services or property (other than cash or notes) is not included in box 2." (lines 77-80). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 4 — Is the box for property or services received as part of the consideration checked?" (yes/no), on every Form 1099-S item; never required. Help text: when it is checked, box 2 understates what the transferor received, and the value of that property or service still belongs in the amount realized. Validation: Boolean. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-S register.

Fact.Name: Form 1099-S box 6, buyer's part of real estate tax
Fact.Description: Form 1099-S box 6, "Buyer's part of real estate tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099s--2025.pdf, page 2). The form's own transferor instruction: "Box 6. Shows certain real estate tax on a residence charged to the buyer at settlement. If you have already paid the real estate tax for the period that includes the sale date, subtract the amount in box 6 from the amount already paid to determine your deductible real estate tax. But if you have already deducted the real estate tax in a prior year, generally report this amount as income on the 'Other income' line of Schedule 1 (Form 1040)." (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/f1099s--2025.pdf, page 4). SCREEN SPEC: ask "Box 6 — Buyer's part of real estate tax" (dollar amount), on every Form 1099-S item; never required. Validation: Dollar, Min $0. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; nothing reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. The Schedule A real-estate-tax apportionment and the Schedule 1 recovery the instruction describes are both stated by the filer on their own lines; this box is the transcription, not either of those legs, and neither is rewired here. Stored for the state and local returns and printed on the Form 1099-S register.
